about: Generated from src/twm/registry.py by `uv run twm glossary --write`; do not edit by hand (tests/test_registry_site.py fails when it is out of date). The site's tooltips (web/components/Term.tsx) read the published glossary table first and this file second, so a term added to the registry has its tooltip as soon as the site deploys, before the next publish. Name, title, explanation and formula only: no reason sentences.

against_convention.title: Against convention
against_convention.explanation: A clear call where the aggressive option was best and the coach took it: he went for it on fourth down, or went for two. The number is how much win probability that gained over the best kicking option, by the model.
against_convention.formula: a clear call with chosen = recommended = go (fourth down) or two-point (try); the number = WP(go) - max(WP(field goal), WP(punt)), or WP(two) - WP(kick)

age.title: Age after the season
age.explanation: How old he is when the season ends; production falls with age, at different ages by position.
age.formula: (February 1 after season S - dim_player.birth_date) / 365.25; NULL without a birth date

age_at_asof.title: Age
age_at_asof.explanation: Younger players are likelier to grow into a bigger role.
age_at_asof.formula: (as-of date - dim_player.birth_date) / 365.25; NULL without a public birth date

age_at_draft.title: Age at the draft
age_at_draft.explanation: Young draftees break out more often: they were productive in college earlier.
age_at_draft.formula: (first day of his draft - birth_date) / 365.25; his entry year's draft when undrafted (available.DRAFT_FIRST_DAY, 2000-2026)

age_curve_ratio.title: Aging curve
age_curve_ratio.explanation: What a typical player of his position and age keeps of his points per game next season, learned only from earlier seasons.
age_curve_ratio.formula: the position's quadratic fit of PPG(s+1) / PPG(s) on age over earlier season pairs (s + 1 <= S; top-48 in s, 6+ games in s+1; 50+ pairs), evaluated at his age (clipped to the fitted ages)

aggressiveness.title: Aggressiveness
aggressiveness.explanation: How often a coach goes for it when the numbers clearly say go.
aggressiveness.formula: clear fourth downs where going for it was best AND the coach went / clear fourth downs where going for it was best (the go rate when go was clearly best)

air_yards_share.title: Air-yards share
air_yards_share.explanation: Air yards are how far the ball travels past the line of scrimmage before it is caught or falls. A big share means a player gets the deep, valuable looks.
air_yards_share.formula: player's receiving air yards / his team's air yards on all pass attempts (completions, incompletions and interceptions) in that game

air_yards_share_avg3.title: Air-yards share, last 3 games
air_yards_share_avg3.explanation: How much of the team's downfield passing is aimed at him.
air_yards_share_avg3.formula: mean nflverse air_yards_share over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game); can be slightly negative (passes behind the line)

air_yards_share_s.title: Air-yards share
air_yards_share_s.explanation: His share of the deep game.
air_yards_share_s.formula: his receiving air yards / his team's in his games of S

all_play_record.title: All-play record
all_play_record.explanation: Your record if you had played every team every week. It shows how good your scores were, whatever the schedule: 9-2 in a week means only two teams scored more than you.
all_play_record.formula: over the regular-season weeks whose games are all final: each week, one win for every other team the team outscored and one loss for every team that outscored it (a tie counts as a tie)

allocation.title: Allocation
allocation.explanation: How much of the missing starter's work a teammate in that role took on average: 0.46 means the backup RB got about 46% of the RB1's carries.
allocation.formula: over past single-starter-out games (2013 on): sum of a role's share changes (game share minus his baseline share) / sum of the vacated shares; shrunk toward its position group with 20 teammate-games; carries only when a RB is out

as_of.title: As-of time
as_of.explanation: The moment a prediction is made. It may only use data that was public by then; the time machine replays any past as-of exactly.
as_of.formula: dim_week.asof_weekly_utc: the first Tuesday 14:00 UTC after the Eastern date of the week's first kickoff (after Monday night for a normal week)

available_at.title: Available at
available_at.explanation: When a row of data became public. A prediction at an as-of time sees only rows with available_at at or before it.
available_at.formula: per table rule in twm.warehouse.available (e.g. game data: estimated game end + 6 h); later when unsure

best_rank.title: Best weekly rank in the window
best_rank.explanation: His best week at his position in the window. A label detail: never a model feature.
best_rank.formula: min(weekly_pos_rank) over the window weeks (NULL if never ranked)

board_cliff_chance.title: Chance of a Cliff
board_cliff_chance.explanation: The model's estimated chance that the player plays enough games next season to judge and loses a large share of his points per game. It is only meaningful for a player who plays: the chance of missing time is a separate number, and the two are never added together.
board_cliff_chance.formula: the pinned Cliff model's own probability of y_cliff (an L2 logistic regression on the preseason features at the kickoff-eve as-of)

board_disagree.title: Where we disagree
board_disagree.explanation: A player near the top of our list for a Cliff who is not among the same number of players the experts' ranking drops furthest below last season's finish, or the reverse. The record of past disagreements shows how both kinds turned out.
board_disagree.formula: ours: the top N of the board by the Cliff chance; theirs: the N players with the largest experts' rank minus last season's position rank by points per game (not ranked first); marked when on one of the two only; nothing without the experts' ranks

board_ecr.title: Experts' preseason rank (ECR)
board_ecr.explanation: FantasyPros' expert consensus ranking: many fantasy experts' preseason ranks at the position, combined into one, from the last scrape before week 1. It is the experts' consensus, not draft position (ADP), and it exists for recent seasons only.
board_ecr.formula: the expert consensus rank at his position on the preseason ranking page of the last scrape before week 1 public by the board's as-of; none when he is not ranked or before the ranking archive's first season

board_kind.title: Live or reconstructed board
board_kind.explanation: A live board is made before the season's first kickoff from the data public then, and never changed afterwards. A reconstructed board (backtest) was scored later, from the data as it stood on the eve of week 1: what the model would have said then, not a board anyone saw at the time.
board_kind.formula: live: scored on the real clock between the board's as-of (the eve of week 1) and the first kickoff, stored once (append-only); backtest: scored later by the pinned models from the input rows as they stood at the as-of

board_missed_chance.title: Chance of missed time
board_missed_chance.explanation: The model's estimated chance that the player plays only a few games next season or none (injury, a benching, a release or retirement), from a separate, simpler model.
board_missed_chance.formula: the pinned missed-time model's own probability of y_missed (a simpler logistic regression on fewer inputs, the same as-of)

brier.title: Brier score
brier.explanation: How close the probabilities came to what happened: the average squared gap between each probability and the outcome (1 if it happened, 0 if not). Lower is better and 0 is perfect. Example: saying 80% for something that happens adds 0.04; saying 80% for something that does not happen adds 0.64.
brier.formula: mean over the rows of (probability - outcome)^2, the outcome 1 when it happened and 0 when not

buy_low.title: Buy-low
buy_low.explanation: He has scored well below what his chances were worth: his points should rise, so he may be cheap to trade for.
buy_low.formula: FPOE/game in the bottom ceil(n / 10) FPOE/game of his position's universe at that as-of AND ppg_ros at least X above his PPG

bye_in_next3.title: Bye in the next 3 weeks
bye_in_next3.explanation: A bye costs a week of production.
bye_in_next3.formula: his team has no scheduled game in at least one of the calendar weeks N+1 to N+3 (capped at the last regular-season week)

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.explanation: Whether probabilities mean what they say: among all players given a similar probability, the share who really hit should be close to that probability.
calibration.formula: the predictions sorted by probability and cut into equal-count groups (10 by default); each group's mean probability is compared with the share of its rows whose outcome happened (perfect calibration: equal)

candidate_pool.title: Waiver Radar candidate pool
candidate_pool.explanation: The players who are probably still on waivers in a typical 12-team league. There is no record of which players sat on fantasy rosters before 2020, so anyone ranked high before the season or scoring well since counts as taken; the rest are the players the Waiver Radar ranks.
candidate_pool.formula: on an NFL roster at the as-of (his latest public weekly roster row of the season, on his team's latest public roster, with status ACT, INA, DEV, at QB/RB/WR/TE) and outside the top N at his position by BOTH preseason_pos_rank and ppg_to_date; N = weekly starter threshold x candidate_pool_multiplier (1.5): QB 18, RB 36, WR 36, TE 18; in seasons without a preseason cheat sheet, rookies drafted in rounds 1-2 count as drafted

career_touches.title: Career touches
career_touches.explanation: Mileage: wear accumulated over a career.
career_touches.formula: carries + receptions in every regular season 1999 .. S (a career before 1999 is cut)

carries.title: Carries
carries.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
carries.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rush_attempt (two-point tries excluded), from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

carry_share.title: Carry share
carry_share.explanation: The share of his team's running plays given to a player: the running-back version of target share.
carry_share.formula: player carries / team carries in that game (fact_player_week.carries / fact_team_week.carries; 0 when the team had no carry)

carry_share_avg3.title: Carry share, last 3 games
carry_share_avg3.explanation: How much of the running game goes to him lately.
carry_share_avg3.formula: mean carry_share over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

carry_share_last.title: Carry share, last game
carry_share_last.explanation: The share of his team's runs he got last game.
carry_share_last.formula: carry_share in the team's last game (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

catch_rate_over_expected.title: Catch rate over expected
catch_rate_over_expected.explanation: How many more of his targets he caught than an average receiver would have.
catch_rate_over_expected.formula: (receptions - receptions_exp) / targets, over the games of one half of a player-season (summed, then divided)

chance.title: Chance
chance.explanation: How often players the Radar rated like him became a fantasy starter soon, in earlier seasons' backtests. The range beside it is how sure that rate is. It is the track record of similar players, not a promise, and not the model's own probability (which ran too high for the top players in the backtest).
chance.formula: the observed y_hit rate of the backtest predictions in the same similar-players bin as his model probability: the walk-forward predictions of the same model and label from the seasons before the list's season, sorted by probability, cut into groups of at least 500 (a probability is never split) and merged so the rate never falls as the probability rises; the range is the bin's 90% Wilson interval

clear_call.title: Clear call
clear_call.explanation: A decision where one option's win probability beat the next best by more than the toss-up margin (Methodology page). Only clear calls are graded: a wrong one counts against the coach.
clear_call.formula: WP(best option) - WP(second best) > decisions.toss_up_margin (config/settings.yaml), every option priced by our win-probability model of that season

clock_case.title: Clock case
clock_case.explanation: A game where one of the three clock-management metrics applies: timeouts unused in a lost one-score game, a passive end of the first half, or seconds wasted late while trailing with timeouts in hand. Each has an exact written definition; situations outside them are never graded.
clock_case.formula: a game where timeouts_unused, half_passivity or timeout_seconds_wasted applies, by its written definition (decisions.clock in config/settings.yaml)

coach_id.title: Coach id
coach_id.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).
coach_id.formula: slug of the head coach's name

combine_speed_score.title: Speed score
combine_speed_score.formula: weight x 200 / forty^4 (Bill Barnwell's Speed Score, Football Outsiders 2008)

completion_rate_over_expected.title: Completion rate over expected (CPOE)
completion_rate_over_expected.explanation: How many more of his passes were completed than an average passer's would have been.
completion_rate_over_expected.formula: (completions - completions_exp) / pass_attempts, over the games of one half of a player-season (summed, then divided)

completions.title: Completions
completions.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
completions.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_completions, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

completions_exp.title: Expected completions
completions_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
completions_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_completions_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

consecutive_losing_seasons.title: Consecutive losing seasons
consecutive_losing_seasons.explanation: How many losing seasons in a row the coach has had with this team before this one.
consecutive_losing_seasons.formula: seasons right before this one, counted back until one is not losing or not coached by him, in which the coach coached the team and its regular-season win share (ties 0.5) was < 0.5

converted.title: Go label: the try converted
converted.explanation: Whether going for it worked: the offense kept the ball with a new set of downs.
converted.formula: third or fourth down pass/run: first_down = 1 or the offense's touchdown, and no interception or lost fumble (defensive penalties that give a first down count)

cpoe.title: CPOE (completion percentage over expected)
cpoe.explanation: Whether a quarterback completes more passes than an average passer would have on the same throws.
cpoe.formula: 1 if the pass was complete else 0, minus nflfastR's expected completion probability, x 100

current_franchise.title: Team
current_franchise.explanation: Teams are shown by today's franchise code and name, also for past seasons: a franchise that moved appears under its current name.
current_franchise.formula: every team column holds today's franchise code (OAK -> LV, SD -> LAC, STL -> LA, LAR -> LA), with today's name

dc_absent.title: Not on a week-1 depth chart
dc_absent.explanation: Cut, unsigned, retired or hurt before the season starts.
dc_absent.formula: no row of his on any team's week-1 depth chart of S+1 visible at the preseason as-of (fact_depth_chart) while his S team's chart is visible; NULL when it is not (dc_team_chart_missing); the other preseason features are then NULL

dc_team_chart_missing.title: No depth chart for his team yet
dc_team_chart_missing.explanation: We cannot tell yet whether he made the team: a missing chart, not a cut.
dc_team_chart_missing.formula: no row of his on any visible week-1 chart of S+1 AND no visible chart of his S team at the preseason as-of (legacy charts are public the Wednesday before week 1; a team whose week-1 game moved has none)

decision_grade.title: Clear call or toss-up
decision_grade.explanation: Only decisions with a clear answer count against a coach.
decision_grade.formula: 'clear' when the best option's WP beats the second best by more than decisions.toss_up_margin (1.5 WP points), else 'toss_up' (not graded); the 4th quarter's last 2:00 and overtime are not graded at all (decisions.late_game)

decisions_graded.title: Decisions
decisions_graded.explanation: Every fourth down and every try after a touchdown the Report Card priced: clear calls and toss-ups together. Kneels, the half's last seconds and snaps wiped out by a penalty are left out.
decisions_graded.formula: fourth downs (2006 on) and tries after a touchdown without an exclusion (not a snap, a penalty with no play, a kneel or spike, an aborted snap, the half's last seconds, the late game, a state the models cannot score): clear calls + toss-ups

def_epa_neutral.title: Defensive EPA per play allowed (neutral)
def_epa_neutral.explanation: How efficient opponents are against this defense; lower is better.
def_epa_neutral.formula: as off_epa_neutral for the opponents' plays against the team (defteam); higher = worse

def_epa_neutral_trend.title: Defensive EPA trend
def_epa_neutral_trend.explanation: Positive: the defense has been allowing more lately than over the whole season.
def_epa_neutral_trend.formula: def_epa_neutral over the last 4 games minus the season to date (NULL until more than 4 games); positive = the defense has been worse lately

defteam.title: Defense team code
defteam.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

defteam_timeouts_remaining.title: Defense timeouts left
defteam_timeouts_remaining.explanation: The other team's timeouts: they can stop the clock to get the ball back.
defteam_timeouts_remaining.formula: the defense's timeouts left in the half, before the snap

depth_listed.title: On the depth chart
depth_listed.explanation: Whether the team lists him at all.
depth_listed.formula: his gsis_id is on his team's chart in force at the as-of in any slot (offense, defense or special teams); NULL when the team has no visible chart

depth_rank_change.title: Depth-chart move
depth_rank_change.explanation: How many spots he moved up the depth chart in a week.

depth_rank_now.title: Depth-chart rank now
depth_rank_now.explanation: Where the team lists him at his position: 1 is the starter.
depth_rank_now.formula: on his team's depth chart in force at the as-of (daily charts 2025+: the team's latest snapshot with dt <= as-of; weekly charts: the latest visible week's chart), 1 + the number of players of his position group with a better (lower) depth rank in any offensive slot of the group; ties share the better rank. Slots map to groups by twm.modules.waiver_radar.features.slot_group (QB; RB, HB, FB, J; WR, LWR, RWR, SWR, WR1/WR2, WRE, WE; TE, LTE, RTE, H-B, F and combined slots with TE). NULL when he is not in a slot of his group

depth_rank_prev.title: Depth-chart rank a week earlier
depth_rank_prev.explanation: Where he was listed a week ago.
depth_rank_prev.formula: depth_rank_now computed from the chart in force 7 days before the as-of

depth_rank_s1.title: Week-1 depth rank
depth_rank_s1.formula: his best depth_rank among his offense slots of his position (RB: RB/HB) on that chart; a daily pull's rank is renumbered within its slot

diff_time_ratio.title: Lead x time played
diff_time_ratio.explanation: The same lead is worth more late in the game; this number grows as time runs out.
diff_time_ratio.formula: score_differential / exp(-4 x elapsed share of regulation; overtime = 1)

division_rank.title: Division rank
division_rank.explanation: Where the team stands in its division right now.
division_rank.formula: rank in the division (dim_team.team_division) by win share (wins + 0.5 ties) / games to date among the division's teams with a game; tied teams share the better rank

doubtful.title: Doubtful
doubtful.explanation: The team says the player is unlikely to play. Since 2016 almost none of the Doubtful QBs, RBs, WRs and TEs took an offensive snap (about 1 in 100).
doubtful.formula: fact_injury_report.report_status = 'Doubtful' on the team's final injury report of the week

down.title: Down
down.explanation: Which of the offense's four tries to gain the distance this is.

draft_pos_best_pick_pd.title: Best pick drafted at his position
draft_pos_best_pick_pd.explanation: How much capital the competition cost.
draft_pos_best_pick_pd.formula: the lowest overall draft_pick among those picks; NULL when there is none

draft_pos_best_round_pd.title: Best round drafted at his position
draft_pos_best_round_pd.explanation: How much capital the competition cost.
draft_pos_best_round_pd.formula: the lowest draft_round among those picks; NULL when there is none

draft_pos_count_pd.title: Draft picks at his position
draft_pos_count_pd.formula: picks of his S team in the S+1 draft (dim_player draft fields, public May 15) whose combine position of that year is his (RB: RB/HB); NULL when no pick is visible

draft_qb_r1_pd.title: Rookie first-round QB
draft_qb_r1_pd.formula: his S team drafted a combine-listed QB in round 1 of the S+1 draft

draft_round.title: Draft round
draft_round.explanation: Teams give early picks more chances.

draft_unplaced_pd.title: Unplaced early pick
draft_unplaced_pd.explanation: The draft counts may miss a pick at his position.
draft_unplaced_pd.formula: his S team made a round 1-3 pick of that draft with no combine row (position unknown point-in-time)

drafted_pick.title: Draft pick
drafted_pick.explanation: Draft capital, finer than the round.

drafted_round.title: Draft round
drafted_round.explanation: Teams give early picks more chances.

drive_value.title: Value of the ball before the half ends
drive_value.explanation: What having the ball here is worth before halftime (or the end), the other team's later possessions included: about 4 points at the opponent's 20 early in a half, about 2 at midfield, 0 when the half ends.
drive_value.formula: half_value(yardline_100, half_seconds_remaining): the offense's points minus the defense's from a 1st down at this spot and clock until halftime, a fixed table measured on the 1999-2005 first halves (wp_data.HALF_VALUE_TABLE), read linearly in yards and log seconds; 0 when the half is over

dst_points_allowed_per_game.title: Points allowed per game (ESPN rule)
dst_points_allowed_per_game.explanation: How many points the defense gives up; fewer points allowed earn more fantasy points.
dst_points_allowed_per_game.formula: mean points_allowed (the opponent's score minus 6 for each touchdown the team's own offense gave up on an interception or fumble return), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game); NULL for K rows

dst_sacks_per_game.title: Sacks per game
dst_sacks_per_game.explanation: How often the defense sacks the quarterback; every sack scores for a team defense.
dst_sacks_per_game.formula: mean def_sacks (half sacks count 0.5), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game); NULL for K rows

dst_takeaways_per_game.title: Takeaways per game
dst_takeaways_per_game.explanation: Interceptions and recovered fumbles: both score for a team defense.
dst_takeaways_per_game.formula: mean (def_interceptions + fumble_recovery_opp), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game); NULL for K rows

dst_tds_per_game.title: Defense and return touchdowns per game
dst_tds_per_game.explanation: Touchdowns scored by the defense or the return teams: rare, but worth a lot.
dst_tds_per_game.formula: mean (kickoff, punt, interception, fumble and blocked-kick return TDs), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game); NULL for K rows

dud_rate.title: Dud rate
dud_rate.explanation: How often a tagged player who did play scored less than half his usual. Healthy players do that too (about 1 in 4), so compare the two numbers.
dud_rate.formula: among tagged players who played, with 2+ earlier games and 5+ points per game so far: share whose points that week were below 50% of their points per game so far; compared with healthy players matched on season, week, position and points-per-game band

early_down_pass_rate.title: Early-down pass rate
early_down_pass_rate.explanation: The neutral pass rate on first and second down only, where the play-caller has the most choice. Higher = passes more on early downs.
early_down_pass_rate.formula: share of neutral 1st-2nd-down snaps that were dropbacks; neutral snap: an offensive snap (pass or run with a down) on downs 1-3 in quarters 1-3 with fact_play.is_neutral

ecr_available.title: Expert ranks available
ecr_available.explanation: Whether the experts' ranking existed at that moment; the expert baseline is only graded where it did.
ecr_available.formula: a rest-of-season or weekly FantasyPros page of the player's roster position of this season is public at the as-of (the archive starts in December 2019)

ecr_page_kind.title: Expert rank source
ecr_page_kind.explanation: Whether the expert rank is a rest-of-season rank or this week's rank.
ecr_page_kind.formula: which page ecr_pos_rank comes from: 'ros' (rest of season) or 'weekly'; NULL when the player is unranked

ecr_pos_rank.title: Expert rank at the as-of
ecr_pos_rank.explanation: How the FantasyPros experts ranked the player at his position at the time. Used only as a baseline to beat (the 'experts' ranking); no model learns from it. Their pages were saved on Fridays, so on Tuesday they had not seen the last weekend's games yet.
ecr_pos_rank.formula: fact_ranking.pos_rank of the player on his roster position's page: the season's latest rest-of-season page public at the as-of if it lists him, else the latest weekly page listing him among those scraped up to twm.modules.waiver_radar.expert_ranks.WEEKLY_MAX_AGE_DAYS days before the latest weekly page; NULL when neither lists him (2020 on)

ecr_scrape_date.title: Expert rank date
ecr_scrape_date.explanation: The day the experts' page was saved.
ecr_scrape_date.formula: scrape_date of the page ecr_pos_rank comes from (public the next day at 00:00 UTC, fact_ranking.available_at)

epa.title: EPA (expected points added)
epa.explanation: How much a single play helped or hurt the offense's scoring chances. A 30-yard catch on 3rd and 10 adds a lot; a sack on 1st down costs points.
epa.formula: nflfastR's expected points after the play minus before it, for the offense

era_kickoff_2023.title: Era: new kickoff rules (2023+)
era_kickoff_2023.explanation: Kickoff rules changed where drives start after a score.
era_kickoff_2023.formula: 1 for seasons 2023 and later (fair-catch touchbacks to the 25 in 2023, the dynamic kickoff from 2024)

era_pat_2015.title: Era: long extra point (2015+)
era_pat_2015.explanation: Extra points got harder in 2015, which slightly changes what a touchdown is worth.
era_pat_2015.formula: 1 for seasons 2015 and later (extra points snapped from the 15-yard line)

espn_id.title: ESPN player id
espn_id.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

expected_wins.title: Market-expected wins to date
expected_wins.explanation: How many games the betting market expected the team to have won by now.
expected_wins.formula: sum over the games to date of the team's pregame win probability: de-vigged closing moneylines p = (1/o_team) / (1/o_team + 1/o_opp) on decimal odds (American +150 -> 2.5, -200 -> 1.5); a game without both moneylines uses 1 / (1 + exp(-k x spread_line)) (home side; k fit by maximum likelihood on every played game of the seasons before, ties out); NULL if a game has neither

fantasy_playoffs.title: Fantasy playoffs
fantasy_playoffs.explanation: The last weeks of the fantasy season, where a loss ends your year: the weeks a manager plans the roster for.
fantasy_playoffs.formula: NFL weeks 15-17 by default (most leagues); My League reads the owner's league settings: the weeks after the regular season, one round per playoff matchup period

fantasy_points.title: Fantasy points
fantasy_points.explanation: The score a player earns for your fantasy team in one game, computed from his yards, touchdowns, catches and mistakes with your league's settings.
fantasy_points.formula: sum over stats of (stat value x points per unit in config/scoring.yaml); full PPR by default

fantasy_points_avg3.title: Fantasy points, last 3 games
fantasy_points_avg3.formula: mean fantasy points over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

fantasy_points_last.title: Fantasy points, last game
fantasy_points_last.formula: fantasy points (config/scoring.yaml) in the team's last game (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

fg_distance.title: Field-goal distance
fg_distance.explanation: How long the kick would be, known before the snap.
fg_distance.formula: yardline_100 + 18 (10 yards of end zone + the hold about 8 yards behind the line; fact_play.kick_distance - yardline_100 is 18 on 88% of 2023-2025 kicks, 19 on 12%)

fg_made.title: FG label: the kick was good
fg_made.explanation: Whether the field goal went through.

flex.title: FLEX
flex.explanation: A week's running back, wide receiver and tight end lists merged into one and ordered by chance. Each chance is the chance of a starter finish at the player's own position, so FLEX compares three slightly different targets: it is a way to browse the three lists together, not a separate model.
flex.formula: the week's RB, WR and TE picks of one kind merged: highest chance first, then the higher model probability, the better rank in his own list, RB/WR/TE and the id; each player once

fourth_down_wp_lost_per_game.title: Fourth-down WP lost per game
fourth_down_wp_lost_per_game.explanation: How much win probability the coach's fourth-down calls have cost per game.
fourth_down_wp_lost_per_game.formula: sum of wp_lost on the team's clear (graded) fourth downs in its games to date / games to date, from the stored Decision Report Card grades (never regraded); NULL before 2006 or when one of the games has no grades

fourth_go_rate.title: Fourth-down go rate
fourth_go_rate.explanation: How often the offense runs a play on fourth down instead of punting or kicking a field goal, in close games. Higher = more aggressive.
fourth_go_rate.formula: share of neutral fourth-down choices where the offense ran a play; fourth-down choice: play_type pass, run, punt, field_goal with fact_play.is_neutral, any quarter; fakes count as going

fourth_short_go_rate.title: Fourth-and-short go rate
fourth_short_go_rate.explanation: The fourth-down go rate on 4th-and-1 or 4th-and-2, where going is most often right. Higher = more aggressive.
fourth_short_go_rate.formula: the same on 4th-and-1 or 4th-and-2; fourth-down choice: play_type pass, run, punt, field_goal with fact_play.is_neutral, any quarter; fakes count as going; ydstogo <= 2

fpoe.title: FPOE (fantasy points over expected)
fpoe.explanation: Points above or below what his chances were worth: partly skill, largely luck, and it tends to shrink toward zero.
fpoe.formula: fantasy_points - xfp (the same player-game; a lost fumble or a return touchdown counts fully, having no expected value); in Regression Watch since H6-b2 and on the player pages since PXFP the xfp is the own walk-forward xFP (own_xfp)

fpoe_avg3.title: FPOE, last 3 games
fpoe_avg3.explanation: Scoring above or below his chances lately; mostly luck, so it is weighted low.
fpoe_avg3.formula: mean over the team's last 3 games of (fantasy_points - xfp) (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

fpoe_ng.title: FPOE without garbage time
fpoe_ng.explanation: Points over expected, counting only plays while the game was in doubt.

fpoe_per_game_s.title: Points over expected per game
fpoe_per_game_s.explanation: Scoring beyond his opportunity, which tends not to last.

game_id.title: Game id
game_id.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

game_seconds_remaining.title: Seconds left in the game
game_seconds_remaining.explanation: How much time is left. A 7-point lead means little early and a lot late.
game_seconds_remaining.formula: seconds left in regulation (in overtime: in the overtime period), before the snap

games.title: Games (G)
games.explanation: How many games a player's numbers are based on. More games make a per-game number more trustworthy: a hot start over 2 games says less than a full season. Example: G 3 with 15 PPG means 45 points over 3 games.
games.formula: the number of games behind the numbers beside it: regular-season games with a stat line in the window shown (on Regression Watch: this season's games up to the as-of, the games behind his PPG, xFP/game and FPOE/game)

games_for_half_weight.title: Games for half weight
games_for_half_weight.explanation: After this many games a player's FPOE/game deserves half its face value.
games_for_half_weight.formula: noise_variance / signal_variance: the g where r(g) = 0.5

games_played_to_date.title: Games played this season
games_played_to_date.explanation: How many games he has a stat line in so far.
games_played_to_date.formula: regular-season games with a stat line visible at the as-of (the pool's games_to_date)

games_remaining.title: Games remaining
games_remaining.explanation: How many regular-season games the team still has to play.
games_remaining.formula: season length (the most regular-season games any team has in the visible schedule) - games played - a listed cancelled game once gone (2022 BUF/CIN after week 17)

games_s.title: Games played
games_s.explanation: How many games he played (with a recorded play).
games_s.formula: regular-season games with a stat line in S

garbage_time_view.title: With or without garbage time
garbage_time_view.explanation: Points, expected points and points over expected either over every play, or only over the plays while the game was still in doubt. Stats piled up once a game is decided say little about next week. The projection itself is the same in both views.
garbage_time_view.formula: with garbage time: points, xFP and FPOE per game over every play; without: points_ng, xfp_ng and fpoe_ng per game (plays with is_garbage_time false only); the projection is computed once and shown in both

gl_opps_avg3.title: Goal-line opportunities per game
gl_opps_avg3.explanation: Chances inside the 10-yard line: the most valuable touches in fantasy.
gl_opps_avg3.formula: mean over the team's last 3 games of his targets plus carries (as above) with yardline_100 <= 10 (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

goal_to_go.title: Goal to go
goal_to_go.explanation: Near the goal line a first down is a touchdown, and the defense has less field to cover.
goal_to_go.formula: 1 when the line to gain is the goal line (fact_play.goal_to_go; for a hypothetical state: ydstogo >= yardline_100)

gsis_id.title: NFL player id
gsis_id.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

half_number.title: Half
half_number.explanation: Which half the play is in. Halftime resets timeouts and gives one team the ball.
half_number.formula: 1 = first half, 2 = second half, 3 = overtime (from fact_play.game_half)

half_passivity.title: End-of-half passivity
half_passivity.explanation: Running out the first half with time, timeouts and field position good enough that attacking was clearly worth points.
half_passivity.formula: a first-half drive that ended the half with a tail of kneels / designed runs (no team timeout, no pass) whose first 1st down had >= 40 s and >= 1 timeout; a case when half_value there >= decisions.clock.passivity_min_ep (1.0 point)

half_seconds_remaining.title: Seconds left in the half
half_seconds_remaining.explanation: Time left before halftime or the end of the game; drives the two-minute drill.
half_seconds_remaining.formula: seconds left in the current half (or overtime period), before the snap

hc_change_s1.title: New head coach (week-1 team)
hc_change_s1.explanation: A new head coach on the team he will play for.
hc_change_s1.formula: his week-1 chart team has a departure with last_season S in coach_departures.csv announced before the as-of's date (blank dates: the hc_departure rule)

hc_departure.title: Head-coach departure
hc_departure.explanation: A new head coach usually means a new offense and new roles.
hc_departure.formula: his S team (his last regular-season game's) has a departure with last_season S in data/manual/coach_departures.csv announced before the snapshot's date (a blank date counts for fired/mutual/interim types only)

hot_seat_driver.title: Drivers
hot_seat_driver.explanation: The three inputs that move this coach's estimate the most, up or down, compared with an average coach: the logistic regression's own terms (its weight times how far the value is from average).
hot_seat_driver.formula: the logistic regression's term of each input: coefficient x standardized value (a value's term and its missing-indicator term summed); the 3 largest by absolute size, signed. A row's terms sum to its log-odds minus the intercept

hot_seat_estimate.title: Estimated chance
hot_seat_estimate.explanation: The model's estimate of the chance that the head coach is let go (fired during or after the season, or a mutual parting) and that it is announced within a set number of days after his team's final game. An estimate from past seasons' patterns, not a prediction that it will happen.
hot_seat_estimate.formula: the live L2 logistic regression's own probability (no recalibration) that the coach is let go (hot_seat_let_go) and it is announced from the row's day through the window's end, a set number of days after his team's final game, playoffs included

hot_seat_let_go.title: Let go
hot_seat_let_go.explanation: Fired during the season, fired after it, or a mutual parting, announced in the window. Other departures (retired, resigned, left for another job) are not counted as let go.
hot_seat_let_go.formula: departure type fired_in_season, fired_after_season or mutual_parting, announced in the window (the owner-verified departures file); retired, resigned (also under pressure) or left for another job: not let go

implied_team_total.title: Implied team total
implied_team_total.explanation: How many points the betting market expected a team to score, from the spread and the over/under. Only known right before kickoff, so P1 uses it for games already played.
implied_team_total.formula: home: (total_line + spread_line) / 2; away: (total_line - spread_line) / 2 (spread_line > 0 = home favored); closing lines of played games only

interceptions.title: Interceptions thrown
interceptions.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
interceptions.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_interception, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

interceptions_exp.title: Expected interceptions
interceptions_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
interceptions_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_interception_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

interval.title: Interval
interval.explanation: The range a number would plausibly move within if the same kind of seasons were played again. It comes from a season-block bootstrap: whole seasons are redrawn at random many times and the number is recomputed each time.
interval.formula: season-block bootstrap: draw as many test seasons as there are, with replacement, recompute the number on the drawn seasons, 2,000 times with a fixed seed, and keep the middle 95%; a difference between two methods is paired (both are graded on the same drawn seasons)

is_first_year_coach.title: First-year coach
is_first_year_coach.explanation: The coach is in his first season with this team.

is_flex_finish.title: FLEX-worthy finish
is_flex_finish.explanation: The running back or receiver scored well enough to fill a FLEX slot that week. Informative only; it is not a label.
is_flex_finish.formula: a RB or WR with weekly_pos_rank <= his position's FLEX-worthy rank (RB/WR top 36); always false for QB and TE

is_fourth_down.title: Fourth down
is_fourth_down.explanation: Separates fourth-down tries (a chosen gamble) from third downs (which add sample).

is_garbage_time.title: Garbage time
is_garbage_time.explanation: Plays after the game is effectively decided. Stats piled up then say little about next week, so views can drop them.
is_garbage_time.formula: win probability below 0.05 or above 0.95, except in the final 120 seconds of a half when the score is within 8 points

is_interim.title: Interim coach (row flag)
is_interim.explanation: Interim coaches are left out of training (spec 8.5). Uses the owner's hindsight file, so it selects rows and is never a model feature.
is_interim.formula: took_over_mid_season OR the owner's data/manual/coach_departures.csv says the coach-team-season was interim (departure_type interim_not_retained or interim_suspected true)

is_neutral.title: Neutral situation
is_neutral.explanation: Plays where the game is still in the balance and neither team is forced to pass or run; the fairest view of how a team really plays.
is_neutral.formula: win probability from 0.2 to 0.8 and more than 120 seconds left in the half

is_rookie.title: Rookie
is_rookie.explanation: First-year players often earn more snaps as the season goes on.
is_rookie.formula: his latest visible roster row's entry_year equals the season

is_second_year_coach.title: Second-year coach
is_second_year_coach.explanation: The coach is in his second season with this team.

is_short_window.title: Short label window
is_short_window.explanation: The window was cut short by the end of the regular season. A label detail: never a model feature.

is_starter_finish.title: Starter finish
is_starter_finish.explanation: The player scored like a weekly starter in a 12-team league that week.
is_starter_finish.formula: weekly_pos_rank <= the position's starter threshold (QB top 12, RB top 24, WR top 24, TE top 12)

is_team_kicker.title: Team's kicker
is_team_kicker.explanation: Whether he is the kicker his team is using now; practice-squad and camp kickers are in the pool but rarely kick.
is_team_kicker.formula: the kicker has a kick attempt in his as-of team's latest visible regular-season game with one (the pool's is_team_kicker; NULL for DST rows)

is_undrafted.title: Undrafted
is_undrafted.formula: no draft round in dim_player at the as-of

joined_team_recently.title: New team this season
joined_team_recently.explanation: He changed teams during the season (trade or signing).
joined_team_recently.formula: his latest visible roster team differs from his earliest roster team this season

k_fg_att_40_plus_per_game.title: Long field-goal attempts per game
k_fg_att_40_plus_per_game.explanation: Long kicks score more fantasy points than short ones in the default scoring.
k_fg_att_40_plus_per_game.formula: field goals made or missed from 40+ yards / games, over the kicker's regular-season games of the season with a field-goal or extra-point attempt visible at the as-of, for any team (NULL for DST rows and for a kicker without one) (blocked kicks have no distance bucket)

k_fg_att_per_game.title: Field-goal attempts per game
k_fg_att_per_game.explanation: How often his team sends him out for field goals: the main source of kicker points.
k_fg_att_per_game.formula: sum of fg_att / games, over the kicker's regular-season games of the season with a field-goal or extra-point attempt visible at the as-of, for any team (NULL for DST rows and for a kicker without one)

k_fg_pct_0_39.title: Field-goal accuracy, 0-39 yards
k_fg_pct_0_39.explanation: How reliable he is on short kicks this season.
k_fg_pct_0_39.formula: fg_made / (fg_made + fg_missed) in the distance bucket, summed over the kicker's regular-season games of the season with a field-goal or extra-point attempt visible at the as-of, for any team (NULL for DST rows and for a kicker without one); blocked kicks are not in nflverse's distance buckets and are left out; NULL without an attempt there (0-19, 20-29 and 30-39 yards)

k_fg_pct_40_49.title: Field-goal accuracy, 40-49 yards
k_fg_pct_40_49.explanation: How reliable he is on medium-long kicks this season.
k_fg_pct_40_49.formula: fg_made / (fg_made + fg_missed) in the distance bucket, summed over the kicker's regular-season games of the season with a field-goal or extra-point attempt visible at the as-of, for any team (NULL for DST rows and for a kicker without one); blocked kicks are not in nflverse's distance buckets and are left out; NULL without an attempt there (40-49 yards)

k_fg_pct_50_plus.title: Field-goal accuracy, 50+ yards
k_fg_pct_50_plus.explanation: How reliable he is from 50 yards and beyond; coaches trust a strong leg with more long tries.
k_fg_pct_50_plus.formula: fg_made / (fg_made + fg_missed) in the distance bucket, summed over the kicker's regular-season games of the season with a field-goal or extra-point attempt visible at the as-of, for any team (NULL for DST rows and for a kicker without one); blocked kicks are not in nflverse's distance buckets and are left out; NULL without an attempt there (50-59 and 60+ yards)

k_pat_att_per_game.title: Extra-point attempts per game
k_pat_att_per_game.explanation: Extra points follow touchdowns, so this shows how often his offense scores.
k_pat_att_per_game.formula: sum of pat_att / games, over the kicker's regular-season games of the season with a field-goal or extra-point attempt visible at the as-of, for any team (NULL for DST rows and for a kicker without one)

kdst_games_to_date.title: K/DST games so far
kdst_games_to_date.explanation: How many games the numbers so far are based on.
kdst_games_to_date.formula: the pool's games_to_date (K: games with a kick attempt; DST: team games)

kdst_points_last.title: K/DST points, latest game
kdst_points_last.explanation: What it scored last time out.
kdst_points_last.formula: fantasy points in the entity's most recent visible regular-season game of the season (K: his latest game with a kick attempt, any team)

kdst_points_per_game.title: K/DST points per game
kdst_points_per_game.explanation: How many fantasy points the kicker or defense has scored per game so far.
kdst_points_per_game.formula: the pool's ppg_to_date: kicking: / defense: points (config/scoring.yaml) per regular-season game visible at the as-of (K: games with a kick attempt; DST: the team's games)

kdst_ppg_rank.title: K/DST points-per-game rank
kdst_ppg_rank.explanation: Where its points per game rank at its position so far.
kdst_ppg_rank.formula: the pool's ppg_pos_rank: rank of kdst_points_per_game among the position's universe with a game (ties share the better rank)

kdst_preseason_rank.title: K/DST preseason rank
kdst_preseason_rank.explanation: Where experts (or last season's scoring) placed it before the season.
kdst_preseason_rank.formula: the pool's preseason_pos_rank: 2020 on the rank on FantasyPros' last August/September K or DST cheat sheet before week 1; earlier the rank by last season's points per game

kickoff_spot.title: Kickoff spot after a score
kickoff_spot.explanation: Where the other team starts after a score (the kickoff rules changed in 2024 and 2025, so it is measured, not assumed).
kickoff_spot.formula: mean receiving start of the same season's kickoffs in earlier weeks (at least decisions.kickoff_min_kicks), else the previous season's, rounded to the yard

kneel_out_seconds.title: Kneel-out seconds K(d, t)
kneel_out_seconds.explanation: The most clock an offense can burn by kneeling from this down; if it is at least the time left, the game is over unless the defense's timeouts cut it.
kneel_out_seconds.formula: n x p + max(0, n - 1 - t) x (g - p), n = 5 - down kneels, t = the defense's timeouts; p (kneel_play) and g (kneel_cycle) = median seconds from a kneel to the next snap with / without a defensive timeout between, measured on the 5 seasons before S

label_status.title: Label status
label_status.explanation: A pending label (the current season) is unknown, never guessed. A label detail: never a model feature.
label_status.formula: 'pending' until every game of every window week has a final score (fact_game.result) and stat lines in the cache, else 'final'

legit.title: Legit (tested, not shown)
legit.explanation: Tested, not shown: a starter whose production is carried by his opportunity, not by luck. It predicted nothing (in the backtest 59.0% of the players it tagged stayed starters, and so did 61.1% of every starter), so the lists do not carry it.
legit.formula: tested, not shown: PPG rank inside the starter threshold (QB top 12, RB top 24, WR top 24, TE top 12) AND FPOE/game not in the top decile of his position's universe; D3's backtest only, dropped from the product on 2026-09-30

list_kind.title: Live or reconstructed
list_kind.explanation: A live list was made in real time on the Tuesday and is never changed afterwards. A reconstructed (backtest) list was made later from the data as it stood on that Tuesday: what the Radar would have said then, not a list anyone saw at the time.
list_kind.formula: live: scored on the real clock after its as-of and before the next kickoff, stored once and never rescored (append-only); backtest (reconstructed): scored later from the data public at the as-of, through the same point-in-time view

listed_position.title: Listed position
listed_position.explanation: The position nflverse lists the player at today, also on his past weekly rows. A Radar list ranks each player at the position of his team's roster that week, which can differ for a player who changed position.
listed_position.formula: nflverse's current position of the player (today's snapshot, also shown on his past rows); a Radar list ranks him at his team's roster position that week

log_loss.title: Log loss
log_loss.explanation: Like the Brier score, it grades probabilities against what happened, but it punishes a confident miss much harder. Lower is better. Example: saying 99% for something that does not happen costs far more than saying 60% for it.
log_loss.formula: mean over the rows of -[y ln(p) + (1 - y) ln(1 - p)], y = 1 when it happened, the probability p kept a hair away from 0 and 1

luck.title: Luck (wins above expected)
luck.explanation: How many more games you won than your scores deserved. +1.5 means the schedule handed you about one and a half extra wins; a negative number means you lost games your points would usually win.
luck.formula: wins (a tie half) - expected wins; expected wins = the sum over the final regular-season weeks of the share of the other teams the team outscored that week (a tie half)

mae.title: Mean absolute error (MAE)
mae.explanation: How far a projection missed on average, whether it was too high or too low. Lower is better. Example: projections of 12 and 8 points per game for two players who both then scored 10 per game miss by 2 each, so the MAE is 2.
mae.formula: mean over the graded players of |actual rest-of-season points per game - the projection|

matchup_gap.title: How much a matchup matters
matchup_gap.explanation: The honest size of the effect: how many points per game really separated players facing the easiest matchups from those facing the hardest, out of sample. The playoff planner's table shows it per position; it is small for most.
matchup_gap.formula: walk-forward 2013-2025: players facing the easiest fifth of matchups (as-of raw rating) minus those facing the hardest fifth, actual minus usual points per game in weeks 15-17

matchup_rating.title: Matchup rating
matchup_rating.explanation: How friendly an opponent is: 1.10 means players at that position scored 10% more than average against it. It moves points a little; for tight ends and kickers the backtest found no gain, so they count as 1.00.
matchup_rating.formula: points the opponent allowed to the position per game this season over the league's average per team-game, shrunk toward 1.00 with k pseudo-games (k by position: QB 33, RB 12, WR 52, TE 100, K 27, DST 8); for a D/ST, the D/ST points the opposing offense gives up; 'adjusted' also divides by what the units it faced usually score

model_probability.title: Model probability
model_probability.explanation: The model's own calibrated probability. The site shows the chance instead: in the backtest the model's probabilities ran too high for the most likely players.
model_probability.formula: the production model's predicted probability of y_hit after an isotonic calibration fit on the validation season (stored as score in the predictions store)

n_flex_finishes.title: FLEX-worthy finishes in the window
n_flex_finishes.explanation: Informative: how often he was worth a FLEX start. A label detail: never a model feature.

n_opp_games_seen.title: Opponent games observed
n_opp_games_seen.explanation: How much evidence the matchup number rests on (little early in the season).
n_opp_games_seen.formula: sum of the visible games of the next opponents used by opp_fp_allowed_next3

n_opportunities.title: Opportunities
n_opportunities.explanation: How many chances he had in the game.
n_opportunities.formula: targets + carries + pass attempts (two-point tries included, sacks not) with an ffopportunity per-play row

n_opportunities_garbage.title: Opportunities in garbage time
n_opportunities_garbage.explanation: How many of his chances came after the game was decided.

n_starter_finishes.title: Starter finishes in the window
n_starter_finishes.explanation: The count behind y_hit and y_sustained. A label detail: never a model feature.

n_window_played.title: Window weeks played
n_window_played.explanation: How many window weeks the player actually took the field on offense. A label detail: never a model feature.
n_window_played.formula: window weeks with fact_snaps.offense_snaps > 0 or a stat line, for any team

neutral_pass_rate.title: Neutral pass rate
neutral_pass_rate.explanation: How often the offense drops back to pass when the game is close and nobody is in a hurry. Higher = passes more; it removes the trailing team throwing and the leading team running out the clock.
neutral_pass_rate.formula: share of neutral 1st-3rd-down snaps that were dropbacks; neutral snap: an offensive snap (pass or run with a down) on downs 1-3 in quarters 1-3 with fact_play.is_neutral

neutral_sec_per_play.title: Neutral pace
neutral_sec_per_play.explanation: Game-clock seconds between snaps in close games. Lower = faster: more plays, more chances for your players. The site shows it as faster than N% of offenses.
neutral_sec_per_play.formula: game-clock seconds between consecutive snaps of a drive, neutral; pace pair: a neutral snap and the same offense's next snap of the drive and quarter with nothing between and no timeout charged; gaps over 60 seconds are clock glitches and dropped

new_competitor_s1.title: New competition
new_competitor_s1.explanation: A rookie or an arrival shares his role.
new_competitor_s1.formula: a same-position teammate at his depth rank or ahead on that chart was on none of that team's regular-season weekly rosters of S

next_is_home.title: Home game next week
next_is_home.explanation: Teams tend to score more and allow less at home.
next_is_home.formula: the as-of team is the home team of its week N+1 game and the venue is not neutral (fact_schedule.location, public from slot_available_at); NULL on a bye or while the venue is not public

next_opp_games_to_date.title: Next opponent: games so far
next_opp_games_to_date.explanation: How many games the opponent numbers are based on.
next_opp_games_to_date.formula: regular-season games with a final score of the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week)

next_opp_giveaways_per_game.title: Next opponent: giveaways per game
next_opp_giveaways_per_game.explanation: An offense that throws interceptions and loses fumbles feeds a defense.
next_opp_giveaways_per_game.formula: mean (def_interceptions + fumble_recovery_opp) of the defenses that faced the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game)

next_opp_points_allowed_per_game.title: Next opponent: points allowed per game
next_opp_points_allowed_per_game.explanation: A defense that gives up many points means more scoring chances for this team.
next_opp_points_allowed_per_game.formula: mean of the scores against the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game)

next_opp_points_per_game.title: Next opponent: points per game
next_opp_points_per_game.explanation: A weak offense next week is a good matchup for a team defense.
next_opp_points_per_game.formula: mean final score of the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game)

next_opp_rz_stall_rate_forced.title: Next opponent: red-zone stall rate forced
next_opp_rz_stall_rate_forced.explanation: A defense that holds teams to field goals in the red zone helps kickers.
next_opp_rz_stall_rate_forced.formula: stalls / trips of offenses facing the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week) (red-zone trip = a drive (fact_play.fixed_drive) with a snap at the opponent's 20 or closer (pass, run, field goal, kneel, spike or a penalty snap; two-point tries excluded); stall = a trip whose drive result is not 'Touchdown'); NULL without a trip

next_opp_rz_trips_allowed_per_game.title: Next opponent: red-zone trips allowed
next_opp_rz_trips_allowed_per_game.explanation: How often offenses reach the red zone against next week's opponent.
next_opp_rz_trips_allowed_per_game.formula: red-zone trips of offenses facing the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week) / its games with play-by-play (red-zone trip = a drive (fact_play.fixed_drive) with a snap at the opponent's 20 or closer (pass, run, field goal, kneel, spike or a penalty snap; two-point tries excluded); stall = a trip whose drive result is not 'Touchdown')

next_opp_sacks_allowed_per_game.title: Next opponent: sacks allowed per game
next_opp_sacks_allowed_per_game.explanation: An offense that gets sacked a lot gives a defense sack points.
next_opp_sacks_allowed_per_game.formula: mean def_sacks of the defenses that faced the entity's as-of team's week N+1 opponent (fact_schedule; NULL on a bye or after the last regular-season week), per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game)

next_venue_dome.title: Next game under a fixed roof
next_venue_dome.explanation: No wind or rain indoors, so kicks are easier.
next_venue_dome.formula: the week N+1 stadium (fact_schedule.stadium_id, used once fact_schedule.stadium is public) has a roof value 'dome' in earlier games visible at the as-of and never open/closed; NULL without an earlier game there

next_venue_retractable.title: Next game under a retractable roof
next_venue_retractable.explanation: A retractable roof is often closed in bad weather.
next_venue_retractable.formula: an earlier visible game at the week N+1 stadium has roof 'open' or 'closed' (the game-day state itself is never used: it is decided on game day); NULL without an earlier game there

ngs_ryoe_per_att_s.title: Rush yards over expected per carry
ngs_ryoe_per_att_s.explanation: Yards gained beyond what the blocking and defenders' positions predicted.
ngs_ryoe_per_att_s.formula: sum(rush_yards_over_expected) / sum(rush_attempts) over his weekly NGS rushing rows of S (games with 10+ carries; 2018 on: upstream has no RYOE for 2016-2017)

ngs_ryoe_trend.title: RYOE trend
ngs_ryoe_trend.explanation: Negative: his running is losing its edge.

ngs_separation_s.title: Separation (Next Gen Stats)
ngs_separation_s.explanation: How open he gets at the catch point; falls as receivers lose speed.
ngs_separation_s.formula: target-weighted mean of avg_separation over his weekly NGS receiving rows of S (games with 5+ targets; 2016 on)

ngs_separation_trend.title: Separation trend
ngs_separation_trend.explanation: Negative: he is getting less open than a year before.

no_huddle_rate.title: No-huddle rate
no_huddle_rate.explanation: How often the offense snaps the ball without huddling first, in close games. Higher = more hurry-up: the cleanest sign of a deliberately fast offense.
no_huddle_rate.formula: share of neutral snaps run no-huddle (from 2006: earlier seasons are not charted); neutral snap: an offensive snap (pass or run with a down) on downs 1-3 in quarters 1-3 with fact_play.is_neutral

noise_variance.title: Noise variance per game
noise_variance.explanation: How much a single game's value swings by luck alone.
noise_variance.formula: var(odd-game mean - even-game mean) / mean(1 / odd games + 1 / even games), across player-seasons of a position

off_epa_neutral.title: Offensive EPA per play (neutral)
off_epa_neutral.explanation: How efficient the offense is when the score does not force its hand.
off_epa_neutral.formula: sum(epa) / plays over the team's run and pass plays (no two-point tries) in neutral situations (fact_play.is_neutral), games to date; plays weighted equally

off_epa_neutral_trend.title: Offensive EPA trend
off_epa_neutral_trend.explanation: Positive: the offense has been better lately than over the whole season.
off_epa_neutral_trend.formula: off_epa_neutral over the team's last hot_seat.trend_games (4) games minus the season to date; NULL until the team has played more than 4 games

offense_snap_share.title: Snap share
offense_snap_share.explanation: How often a player was on the field when his team had the ball. Coaches reveal their plans through snaps before the box score does.
offense_snap_share.formula: fact_snaps.offense_pct: the player's offensive snaps divided by his team's offensive snaps in that game (Pro Football Reference, rounded to 0.01)

opp_fp_allowed_next3.title: Next opponents' points allowed
opp_fp_allowed_next3.explanation: Whether his next matchups are soft (above 1) or tough (below 1) for his position.
opp_fp_allowed_next3.formula: mean over his team's next 3 scheduled opponents (fact_schedule weeks after N, byes skipped; the listed cancelled games count until played) of: fantasy points the opponent's defense allowed per game to his position group this season (visible games; the scorer's snap-count position of that game, else his latest roster position) / the league average per team-game for the group; an opponent without a visible game counts 1.0; NULL when his team has no game left. No betting lines (spec 6.4)

own_wp.title: Win probability (our model)
own_wp.explanation: The chance the offense wins from this moment, from a model that never saw the season it scores. It replaces nflfastR's wp in the decision grades.
own_wp.formula: trained walk-forward on seasons before the play's season (G1); since G1b a smooth possession-symmetric spline logistic model of the play state up to 15:00 of the fourth quarter, handing over to a monotone LightGBM by 10:00 left (wp_select.CHOSEN); isotonic calibration only where it helped on the validation season and kept the model within the smoothness limits

own_xfp.title: Own walk-forward xFP
own_xfp.explanation: Regression Watch's expected points since 2026-10-01 and the player pages' since 2026-10-02: the same idea as nflverse's ffopportunity, but each season is valued by models that never saw it or any later season, so a backtest cannot borrow from the future.
own_xfp.formula: xfp from the project's own per-play models (catch chance, yards after the catch, pass touchdown and interception chances per target; yards and touchdown chance per carry; two-point success rates), LightGBM or a spline GLM per part, for a play of season S trained only on seasons 2006 to S-1; inputs are the situation before the snap (air yards, field position, down and distance, direction, quarter, score), never an nflfastR model column; scored with D1's per-play rules and config/scoring.yaml. The current season's models are pinned with their sha256 (config/production_models.yaml) and only loaded by the weekly job; the player pages' earlier seasons are frozen in the same pin (player_xfp)

owned_avg.title: Rostership (percent of leagues)
owned_avg.explanation: How many real leagues have the player on a roster. It checks the candidate pool (a player owned in fewer than 50% of leagues is really available); the pool itself never uses it, because it does not exist before 2020.
owned_avg.formula: FantasyPros' average share of leagues rostering the player across sites (fact_ranking.player_owned_avg) from the season's latest weekly ranking public at the as-of (the Friday before that week's games); owned_espn = ESPN's share (fact_ranking.player_owned_espn). 2020 partly, 2021 on

p_convert.title: Conversion probability
p_convert.explanation: The chance that going for it on this down and distance works.
p_convert.formula: LightGBM on the go-for-it features, trained walk-forward (seasons < S)

p_fg_make.title: Field-goal probability
p_fg_make.explanation: The chance the kick is good from here, in these conditions.
p_fg_make.formula: LightGBM on distance, roof, wind, temperature, surface and era, walk-forward

pass_attempts.title: Pass attempts
pass_attempts.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
pass_attempts.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_attempt (sacks and two-point tries excluded), from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

passing_tds.title: Passing touchdowns
passing_tds.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
passing_tds.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_touchdown, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

passing_tds_exp.title: Expected passing touchdowns
passing_tds_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
passing_tds_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_touchdown_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

passing_yards.title: Passing yards
passing_yards.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
passing_yards.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_yards_gained, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

passing_yards_exp.title: Expected passing yards
passing_yards_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
passing_yards_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.pass_yards_gained_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

passivity_ep_left.title: EP left on the table (end of half)
passivity_ep_left.explanation: How many points, net of the risk, a typical team got from that spot and clock.
passivity_ep_left.formula: G1b half_value(yardline_100, half_seconds_remaining) at the decision snap minus 0 (kneeling scores nothing): net points from a first-half 1st down to halftime, measured on 1999-2005

passivity_wp_left.title: WP left on the table (end of half)
passivity_wp_left.explanation: What running out the half cost in win probability, by the model.
passivity_wp_left.formula: WP(decision snap) - WP(the second half's first snap: same score, 3 timeouts each, the receiving team at the kickoff spot), both from season S's own WP fold model

pat_rate.title: Extra-point rate
pat_rate.explanation: How often the kick after a touchdown is good.
pat_rate.formula: made extra points / attempts in the last 5 seasons before S within the same rule era (2015+: from the 15)

pfr_player_id.title: Pro Football Reference id
pfr_player_id.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

play_chance.title: Chance he plays
play_chance.explanation: Out of 100 players like him in past seasons, about this many played. Teams name their inactive players about 90 minutes before kickoff: check then.
play_chance.formula: share of past tagged players with the same tag, position and 'missed his team's previous game' who took at least one offensive snap (fact_snaps), seasons 2016 to last season, each group shrunk toward its parent group (20 pseudo-rows)

play_points.title: Fantasy points added up play by play
play_points.explanation: The same points as the weekly stat line, credited play by play so a game can be split into parts; equal to fantasy_points for 99.9% of player-games.
play_points.formula: the sum over his plays of each play's stats scored with config/scoring.yaml (twm.scoring.score_sql): passer = passing yards, passing touchdown, interception; target = reception, receiving yards; rusher = rushing yards; lateral receiver or rusher = the lateral's yards; td_player_id = the touchdown (rushing, receiving, return or fumble-recovery); two-point conversions to the passer, target or rusher of the try; a lost fumble to the player who lost it

play_xfp.title: xFP added up play by play
play_xfp.explanation: The same expected points as the weekly xFP, counted play by play (equal within rounding).
play_xfp.formula: the sum over his plays of ffopportunity's per-play expected stats scored like xfp: a pass is worth pass_completion_exp catches (completions for the passer) and pass_completion_exp x (air_yards + yards_after_catch_exp) yards plus pass_touchdown_exp (and, for the passer, pass_interception_exp); a run rush_yards_exp and rush_touchdown_exp; a two-point try only two_point_conv_exp

player_id.title: Player id (player_stats)
player_id.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

player_season.title: Player-season
player_season.explanation: One player's regular season. The stability study counts each season he played enough games in once, at the position of most of his games, and splits his games into two halves.
player_season.formula: a QB, RB, WR or TE's regular season (2009 on) with at least 8 games with an opportunity (a target, carry or pass), at the position of most of his games; his games split odd/even and first/second half

playoff_odds.title: Playoff odds
playoff_odds.explanation: Your chance to make the playoffs, from playing out the rest of the season thousands of times on your real schedule. Early in the season it leans on the league average, so it moves a lot week to week. Local only.
playoff_odds.formula: share of 20,000 seeded simulated seasons in which the team finishes in the playoff places: every remaining matchup on the real schedule, each team's weekly score drawn around its season mean shrunk toward the league mean (6 pseudo-weeks), seeded by record then ESPN's tiebreak, then the playoff bracket (docs/my_league.md)

point_diff_per_game.title: Point differential per game
point_diff_per_game.explanation: By how much the team outscores (or is outscored by) its opponents on average.
point_diff_per_game.formula: (points scored - points allowed) / games, regular season to date

points_garbage.title: Fantasy points in garbage time
points_garbage.explanation: Points he scored after the game was effectively decided.
points_garbage.formula: the fantasy points of his garbage-time plays (fact_play.is_garbage_time), credited play by play as in play_points

points_ng.title: Fantasy points without garbage time
points_ng.explanation: The points he scored while the game was still in doubt. Late points in a blowout come against soft defenses and say little about next week.
points_ng.formula: fantasy_points - points_garbage: the weekly stat line's points minus those scored on his garbage-time plays (fact_play.is_garbage_time)

points_per_opportunity.title: Points per opportunity
points_per_opportunity.explanation: How much he scores with each carry or target; more work times this gives the predicted points.
points_per_opportunity.formula: his PPR points / (carries + targets) over his baseline games, with 20 opportunities at his position's past average added

pos_rank_s.title: PPG rank at his position
pos_rank_s.explanation: Where he finished; also the prior-season-rank baseline's only input.
pos_rank_s.formula: rank by ppg_s among his position's players with 8+ games in S (ties: more points, then id); NULL under 8 games

pos_rb.title: Running back
pos_rb.explanation: Position flag (QB is the case with every flag off). A category, not an identifier.
pos_rb.formula: his point-in-time position in S is RB

pos_te.title: Tight end
pos_te.formula: his point-in-time position in S is TE

pos_wr.title: Wide receiver
pos_wr.formula: his point-in-time position in S is WR

position.title: Position
position.explanation: Which position he plays; hit rates differ by position. A category, not an identifier.
position.formula: his point-in-time roster position (the pool's position)

posteam.title: Offense team code
posteam.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

posteam_is_home.title: Offense at home
posteam_is_home.explanation: Home teams win a bit more often; neutral-site games (London, Super Bowl) have no home team.
posteam_is_home.formula: 1 when the possession team is the home team, 0 when away, 0.5 at a neutral site (fact_game.location)

posteam_spread.title: Pregame spread (offense's view)
posteam_spread.explanation: How many points the betting market expected the team with the ball to win by, set right before kickoff (allowed: it is known when the game starts).
posteam_spread.formula: closing spread_line if the possession team is home, else minus spread_line (spread_line > 0 = home favored): the margin the market expected for the offense

posteam_timeouts_remaining.title: Offense timeouts left
posteam_timeouts_remaining.explanation: Timeouts stop the clock: a trailing team with timeouts has more time to come back.
posteam_timeouts_remaining.formula: the possession team's timeouts left in the half, before the snap

posteam_wins.title: WP label: the team with the ball won
posteam_wins.explanation: What the win-probability model learns to predict, play by play.
posteam_wins.formula: 1 when the possession team before the snap won the game (fact_game.result from its side > 0), 0 when it lost; tie games are left out

ppg.title: Points per game (PPG)
ppg.explanation: A player's fantasy points divided by the games he played: what he scores in a typical game. Higher is better for your team. Example: 45 points in 3 games is 15 PPG.
ppg.formula: fantasy points (config/scoring.yaml) summed over the games counted / the number of those games (each page says which games: e.g. this season so far, or last season)

ppg_change.title: PPG change
ppg_change.explanation: A big jump is likely to give some back.
ppg_change.formula: ppg_s - PPG in S-1 (NULL without S-1)

ppg_pos_rank.title: PPG rank at his position
ppg_pos_rank.explanation: Where his points per game rank at his position so far.
ppg_pos_rank.formula: rank of ppg_to_date within his roster position among roster players with a game (ties share the better rank; the candidate pool's ppg_pos_rank)

ppg_ros.title: Rest-of-season projection
ppg_ros.explanation: The points per game we expect for the rest of the season: his opportunity, plus the small part of his luck-or-skill surplus that tends to last.
ppg_ros.formula: recency-weighted xFP/game + r(g) x FPOE/game (spec: shrink toward 0) or m + r(g) x (FPOE/game - m) (toward the position's average m); r(g) = shrinkage_factor after his g games with an opportunity, estimated only on seasons before this one; the variant (target, half-life, garbage time) is chosen on earlier seasons (docs/regression_watch.md)

ppg_s.title: Points per game
ppg_s.formula: regular-season fantasy points in S (config/scoring.yaml) / games_s

ppg_to_date.title: Points per game this season
ppg_to_date.explanation: How much a player has scored per game so far this season. A player near the top has been picked up by now, so he is not in the candidate pool.
ppg_to_date.formula: fantasy points (config/scoring.yaml) summed over the season's regular-season games public at the as-of / the number of those games (weeks with a stat line); ppg_pos_rank ranks it within the roster position (ties share the better rank)

ppr.title: PPR (points per reception)
ppr.explanation: A scoring format that gives a point for every catch, on top of yards and touchdowns, which makes pass-catchers more valuable.
