ppr.formula: config/scoring.yaml receiving.receptions (1 = full PPR, 0.5 = half, 0 = standard)

pr_auc.title: PR-AUC
pr_auc.explanation: How cleanly the top of a model's list is filled with the cases that really happened, for rare events. Higher is better, but guessing does not score 0.5: a random order scores the share of cases that happened. Example: if 1 player in 4 really fell off a cliff, a random order scores about 0.25, and a useful model clearly more.
pr_auc.formula: average precision: the precision at each case that happened, going down the list from the highest probability, averaged over those cases (the area under the precision-recall curve)

practice_status.title: Practice status
practice_status.explanation: How much he practiced late in the week. Shown for context only: the 2025+ injury data no longer matches earlier seasons here, so the chance does not use it.
practice_status.formula: fact_injury_report.practice_status of the week's final report: Full Participation, Limited Participation, Did Not Participate (blank: none)

precision_at_10.title: Precision@10
precision_at_10.explanation: The share of a list's top 10 who became a fantasy starter soon (a hit). If you had picked up the top 10 at a position that week, it is the share that would have given you a starter week. The track record averages it over every weekly list.
precision_at_10.formula: per weekly list: players among its top 10 with y_hit / 10 (a list with fewer than 10 players divides by its size); pooled = the mean over every list (weeks x positions) of the seasons

preseason_pos_rank.title: Preseason position rank
preseason_pos_rank.explanation: Where the player stood before the season: experts' consensus ranking (ECR) when it exists, otherwise last season's scoring. A player ranked high was drafted in almost every league.
preseason_pos_rank.formula: 2020 on (method ecr): the player's rank among his position's players on FantasyPros' last August/September redraft cheat sheet of that position before the season's first game (fact_ranking.pos_rank, page_kind preseason); not on his roster position's sheet: his rank on his own FantasyPros position's sheet, judged against that position's cutoff. 2013-2019 (method prior_ppg): his rank by last season's regular-season PPG among players of his current roster position with at least 4 games; ties share the better rank

preseason_ranked.title: Ranked before the season
preseason_ranked.explanation: Whether any preseason list ranked him at all.
preseason_ranked.formula: preseason_pos_rank is not NULL (FantasyPros ECR 2020 on; last season's PPG rank or a round 1-2 rookie before)

prev_playoff_result.title: Previous playoff result (text)
prev_playoff_result.explanation: Last season's playoff exit, spelled out.
prev_playoff_result.formula: prev_playoff_round as text: none, lost_wc, lost_div, lost_conf, lost_sb, won_sb

prev_playoff_round.title: Previous season playoff result
prev_playoff_round.explanation: How far the team went in last season's playoffs.
prev_playoff_round.formula: last season: 0 no playoffs, 1 lost wild card, 2 lost divisional, 3 lost conference, 4 lost Super Bowl, 5 won it (text in prev_playoff_result)

prev_season_wins.title: Previous season wins
prev_season_wins.explanation: How the team did last year.
prev_season_wins.formula: the team's regular-season wins last season (ties 0.5), whoever coached; NULL for a team without games last season

prior_mean.title: Average FPOE per game (prior)
prior_mean.explanation: The value a shrunk FPOE/game is pulled toward when shrinking toward the position average instead of zero.
prior_mean.formula: sum of FPOE over sum of games, over the player-seasons of a position

prior_seasons.title: Prior seasons
prior_seasons.explanation: Experience; the Cliff needs 3+, the Breakout 0 or 1.
prior_seasons.formula: S - fact_roster_week.entry_year (= years_exp): his seasons in the league before S

priority.title: Suggested priority
priority.explanation: A suggestion from the chance: must-add, speculative or watch. The cutoffs, and how often each priority hit in the backtest, are on the Methodology page.
priority.formula: from the chance, for the top 25 of a list: must-add when it is at least 0.50, speculative from 0.25 up to that, watch below; ranks 26 and lower get none. The bins only go up, so each priority is a cutoff on the model probability

proe.title: Pass rate over expected (PROE)
proe.explanation: How much more often the offense passes than an average team would in the same down, distance, field position, score and clock. Higher = passes more than expected; 0 = league-typical; negative = runs more than expected.
proe.formula: pass rate over expected: mean nflfastR pass_oe (percentage points) over offensive snaps where it is defined, all situations (from 2006: earlier seasons are not charted); every situation: nflfastR's expected pass rate already models down, distance, field position, score, clock and win probability

projection_range.title: 80% range
projection_range.explanation: Where his rest-of-season points per game should land 8 times in 10: the projection plus how far off it was for similar players in earlier seasons. In the backtest the real result fell inside about 80% of the time at every position (the Methodology page shows each share); it says nothing about games he misses.
projection_range.formula: ppg_ros + the 10th and 90th percentiles of the frozen backtest's per-game misses (rest_of_season_ppg - ppg_ros) at his position, from lists with weeks left within 2 of his list's (else the nearest weeks left), of seasons before the list's only (walk-forward); none with fewer than 30 misses

pseudo_games.title: Pseudo-games (shrinkage)
pseudo_games.explanation: A few games say little about a defense, so its rating starts at average and moves away only as real games pile up.
pseudo_games.formula: k imaginary games at exactly average added to a team's record: rating = (allowed + k x average) / ((games + k) x average); k = within-team over between-team variance, estimated on 2006-2012

punt_expected_wp.title: Expected WP after a punt
punt_expected_wp.explanation: How good punting is, as a win chance, averaged over where punts from this spot really end up.
punt_expected_wp.formula: sum over the smoothed empirical distribution of punt results (receiving team's spot, kicking team recovers, return touchdown) of the kicking team's own WP (G1) in the resulting state

pythag_minus_wins.title: Pythagorean wins minus wins
pythag_minus_wins.explanation: Positive: the team has been unlucky in close games; negative: lucky.

pythagorean_wins.title: Pythagorean wins
pythagorean_wins.explanation: The wins a team 'deserves' from its points scored and allowed.
pythagorean_wins.formula: games x PF^e / (PF^e + PA^e), e = hot_seat.pythagorean_exponent (2.37, the NFL exponent Football Outsiders uses); NULL when PF + PA = 0

qb1_change_s1.title: New starting QB
qb1_change_s1.explanation: A new quarterback changes the targets.
qb1_change_s1.formula: the team's S primary starter (most regular-season pass attempts for it in S) is not among its best-ranked QBs on that chart

questionable.title: Questionable
questionable.explanation: The team says the player is uncertain to play. Since 2016 about 6 in 10 Questionable QBs, RBs, WRs and TEs played; the list shows the chance for players like him.
questionable.formula: fact_injury_report.report_status = 'Questionable' on the team's final injury report of the week (2016 on: the NFL's definition since dropping Probable)

rank_bucket_hit_rate.title: Hit rate by rank
rank_bucket_hit_rate.explanation: How often players ranked this high hit, counted over earlier reconstructed lists of the same position (seasons before this list's season, so the badge never uses outcomes the list could not have known).
rank_bucket_hit_rate.formula: hits / picks at ranks 1-5, 6-10 or 11-25 of the reconstructed (backtest) lists of the same position, over the seasons before the list's season

receives_2h_kickoff.title: Gets the ball after halftime
receives_2h_kickoff.explanation: In the first half, knowing you get the ball back after halftime is worth a little.
receives_2h_kickoff.formula: first half only: 1 when the possession team kicked the opening kickoff (it receives the second-half kickoff); 0 in the second half and overtime

receiving_tds.title: Receiving touchdowns
receiving_tds.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
receiving_tds.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rec_touchdown, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

receiving_tds_exp.title: Expected receiving touchdowns
receiving_tds_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
receiving_tds_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rec_touchdown_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

receiving_yards.title: Receiving yards
receiving_yards.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
receiving_yards.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rec_yards_gained, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

receiving_yards_exp.title: Expected receiving yards
receiving_yards_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
receiving_yards_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rec_yards_gained_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

recency_weighted_xfp.title: Recency-weighted xFP per game
recency_weighted_xfp.explanation: His expected points per game, with recent games counting a little more.
recency_weighted_xfp.formula: sum of 0.5 ** (k / h) x xFP over his games this season / sum of 0.5 ** (k / h), k = games before his latest one, h = the half-life (none / 8 / 4 / 2 games; chosen per season on earlier seasons)

receptions.title: Receptions
receptions.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
receptions.formula: fact_opportunity_week.receptions, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

receptions_exp.title: Expected receptions
receptions_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
receptions_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.receptions_exp: the sum of the completion chances of his targets, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

reg_games_played.title: Games played to date
reg_games_played.explanation: How many games the team has played so far this season.
reg_games_played.formula: the team's played regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (fact_game)

reg_wins.title: Wins to date
reg_wins.explanation: The team's wins so far, ties counting as half a win.
reg_wins.formula: regular-season wins to date, a tie = 0.5

regression_to_the_mean.title: Regression to the mean
regression_to_the_mean.explanation: A player who scores far above his opportunity usually comes back down; one who scores far below usually rises. Opportunity is 'stickier' than efficiency.
regression_to_the_mean.formula: extreme results drift back toward the average when luck made them extreme

regression_universe.title: Regression Watch universe
regression_universe.explanation: The fantasy-relevant players Regression Watch projects and tags each week.
regression_universe.formula: QB/RB/WR/TE with at least 3 games so far whose PPG or xFP/game ranks inside teams x (starting slots the position can fill, FLEX included) x 1.5: QB 18, RB 54, WR 54, TE 36

reliability.title: Reliability after g games
reliability.explanation: The share of a g-game average that is real rather than luck; it grows with g.

rest_of_season_ppg.title: Rest-of-season PPG (actual)
rest_of_season_ppg.explanation: What he really scored per game afterwards: what the projection is graded on.
rest_of_season_ppg.formula: fantasy points per game over his regular-season games public after the as-of (graded only with at least 3 such games)

roc_auc.title: ROC-AUC
roc_auc.explanation: How well a model puts the cases that happened above the ones that did not. 0.5 is no better than guessing and 1 is a perfect order, so higher is better. Example: 0.80 means that in 8 of 10 pairs of one coach who was let go and one who was not, the model gave the first a higher estimate.
roc_auc.formula: the probability that a random row whose outcome happened gets a higher probability than a random row whose outcome did not (ties count half): the area under the ROC curve, over the pooled walk-forward test rows

roof_closed.title: Indoors
roof_closed.formula: 1 when fact_game.roof is dome or closed; 0 for outdoors, open or unknown

rookie_r1_qb_on_roster.title: Rookie first-round QB
rookie_r1_qb_on_roster.explanation: The team drafted its quarterback of the future: owners tend to be patient.
rookie_r1_qb_on_roster.formula: a QB (fact_roster_week.position) on the team's latest visible weekly roster of the season (status not CUT/RET/UFA/TRD) was a first-round pick of this year's draft (dim_player draft_round = 1, draft_year = season); NULL without a visible roster

routes_proxy_avg3.title: Routes proxy
routes_proxy_avg3.explanation: About how many pass plays he was on the field for: a stand-in for routes run, which nflverse does not publish.
routes_proxy_avg3.formula: mean over the team's last 3 games of (team dropbacks in the game x his snap share in it); dropbacks = plays with qb_dropback = 1 that are not two-point tries (passes, sacks, scrambles) (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

rush_share_s.title: Rush share
rush_share_s.explanation: His share of the running game.
rush_share_s.formula: his carries / his team's carries in his games of S

rushing_tds.title: Rushing touchdowns
rushing_tds.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
rushing_tds.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rush_touchdown, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

rushing_tds_exp.title: Expected rushing touchdowns
rushing_tds_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
rushing_tds_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rush_touchdown_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

rushing_yards.title: Rushing yards
rushing_yards.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
rushing_yards.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rush_yards_gained, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

rushing_yards_exp.title: Expected rushing yards
rushing_yards_exp.explanation: What an average player would have produced from the same chances; compare with the actual number to see efficiency.
rushing_yards_exp.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rush_yards_gained_exp, from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

rz_carries_avg3.title: Red-zone carries per game
rz_carries_avg3.formula: mean over the team's last 3 games of his runs (play_type run, not two-point tries; kneels excluded) with yardline_100 <= 20 (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

rz_targets_avg3.title: Red-zone targets per game
rz_targets_avg3.explanation: Targets inside the opponent's 20-yard line, where touchdowns come from.
rz_targets_avg3.formula: mean over the team's last 3 games of his targets on pass plays (not two-point tries) with yardline_100 <= 20 (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

same_pos_vacated_carry_share.title: Vacated carry share at his position
same_pos_vacated_carry_share.explanation: Carries freed up by players at his own position.
same_pos_vacated_carry_share.formula: vacated_carry_share over unavailable teammates of his own position group only

same_pos_vacated_target_share.title: Vacated target share at his position
same_pos_vacated_target_share.explanation: Targets freed up by players at his own position: the most direct path to more work.
same_pos_vacated_target_share.formula: vacated_target_share over unavailable teammates of his own position group only

score_differential.title: Score difference (offense minus defense)
score_differential.explanation: How far ahead (positive) or behind (negative) the team with the ball is.
score_differential.formula: possession team's score minus the defense's, before the snap

sell_high.title: Sell-high
sell_high.explanation: He has scored well above what his chances were worth, and the projection says it will fade: a good time to trade him away.
sell_high.formula: FPOE/game in the top ceil(n / 10) FPOE/game of his position's universe at that as-of AND ppg_ros at least X (tag_threshold_x) below his PPG

shotgun_rate.title: Shotgun rate
shotgun_rate.explanation: How often the quarterback lines up a few yards behind the center (shotgun) in close games. Higher = more spread-out, pass-ready formations.
shotgun_rate.formula: share of neutral snaps from shotgun; neutral snap: an offensive snap (pass or run with a down) on downs 1-3 in quarters 1-3 with fact_play.is_neutral

shrinkage_factor.title: Shrinkage factor
shrinkage_factor.explanation: How much of a player's points over expected to keep when projecting the rest of the season; the rest is expected to fade.
shrinkage_factor.formula: reliability r(g) of FPOE/game for his position after his g games, estimated only from seasons before the one projected (stability.shrinkage(seasons))

signal_variance.title: Signal variance
signal_variance.explanation: How much players truly differ in the metric once luck is taken out.
signal_variance.formula: covariance, across player-seasons of a position, of FPOE/game in his odd games and in his even games

snap_pct_s.title: Snap share
snap_pct_s.explanation: How much of the time he is on the field.
snap_pct_s.formula: mean fact_snaps.offense_pct over his regular-season games with an offensive snap in S (2013 on; NULL before)

snap_share_avg3.title: Snap share, last 3 games
snap_share_avg3.explanation: His usual playing time lately, less noisy than one game.
snap_share_avg3.formula: mean offense_snap_share over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

snap_share_delta.title: Snap share change
snap_share_delta.explanation: Did his playing time just go up or down? A big rise means the coaches trust him more.
snap_share_delta.formula: snap_share_last minus the mean snap share of the up to 3 team games before the last (NULL when the last game is the team's first)

snap_share_last.title: Snap share, last game
snap_share_last.explanation: How much he played in the most recent game. A jump is often the first sign of a bigger role.
snap_share_last.formula: offense_snap_share in the team's last game (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

snap_share_season.title: Snap share, season
snap_share_season.explanation: His playing time over the whole season so far.
snap_share_season.formula: mean offense_snap_share over all team games of the season (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

split_half_correlation.title: Split-half correlation
split_half_correlation.explanation: How much a number repeats within a season: near 1 it is a lasting trait (role or skill), near 0 it was mostly luck.
split_half_correlation.formula: Pearson correlation, across player-seasons (8+ games with a target, carry or pass; 2009 on; one position per player-season), of a metric in one half of his games with the same metric in the other half: odd against even games, or his first n // 2 games against the rest

spread_time.title: Spread x time left
spread_time.explanation: The pregame expectation fades as the game goes on; this lets the model weigh it less and less.
spread_time.formula: posteam_spread x exp(-4 x elapsed share of regulation; overtime = 1)

stability_interval.title: Interval (stability study)
stability_interval.explanation: The range the number would plausibly move within with other players: the player-seasons are redrawn at random many times and the number is recomputed each time. The same player appears in several seasons, so the true range is a little wider.
stability_interval.formula: bootstrap over player-seasons: redraw them with replacement 1,000 times, recompute the split-half correlation each time and keep the middle 95%

start_sit_odds.title: Start/sit odds
start_sit_odds.explanation: Choosing between two players? This is how often a player ranked like the first outscored one ranked like the second. Under 55% it is a close call: either is a reasonable start. Local only: it uses the experts' weekly ranks, which may not be republished.
start_sit_odds.formula: P(A outscores B) for independent draws of the league points of players at A's and B's weekly expert ranks in 2020-2025 (each rank pooled with its neighbours), a tie counting one half; walk-forward checked on 2022-2025 (docs/start_sit.md)

starter_out.title: Starter out
starter_out.explanation: One of the team's main ball carriers or pass catchers misses the game, so his carries and targets go to someone else.
starter_out.formula: a RB with a carry share of 45%+ or a WR/TE with a target share of 20%+ over the games he played among his team's previous 4 (at least 2) who takes no offensive snap while still on the team (traded, released and retired players do not count); live: Out or Doubtful on the week's injury report, or on a reserve list (IR, PUP ...)

starter_threshold.title: Weekly starter threshold
starter_threshold.explanation: A player 'finished as a starter' in a week when he scored well enough that a typical 12-team league would have started him.
starter_threshold.formula: teams x dedicated starters at the position (derived from config/league.yaml teams and lineup): QB top 12, RB top 24, WR top 24, TE top 12 by fantasy points that week; FLEX-worthy (teams x (dedicated starters + multi-position slots the position can fill), for the positions in flex_worthy_positions): RB/WR top 36

starting_qb_changes.title: Starting-QB changes
starting_qb_changes.explanation: How many different quarterbacks beyond the first have started this season.
starting_qb_changes.formula: distinct starting QBs (fact_game home/away_qb_id) in the games to date minus 1

stream_chance.title: Chance (K and D/ST)
stream_chance.explanation: How often picks the streamer rated alike scored like a starter the very next week, in earlier seasons' backtests: for kickers, picks with a similar model score; for team defenses, the rule's pick at the same rank. The range beside it is how sure that rate is. A track record, not a promise.
stream_chance.formula: read off the frozen streamer backtest of the seasons before the list's season: kickers: the y_start rate of the bin of backtest picks with a similar model score (bins of at least 200 picks); D/STs: the y_start rate of the rule's picks at that rank (rank bins of at least 100 picks); a better score or rank never shows a lower chance; 90% interval

stream_pool.title: Streaming pool
stream_pool.explanation: The kickers and team defenses who are probably still on waivers: those ranked low both by the experts before the season and by points per game so far. It is an estimate, the same kind as the Waiver Radar's candidate pool, because past waiver wires are not public.
stream_pool.formula: the Waiver Radar's candidate-pool rule for K and D/ST: outside the pool cutoff both in the experts' preseason ranking (last season's points per game before 2020) and in points per game so far this season

strength_of_schedule.title: Strength of schedule
strength_of_schedule.explanation: How easy or hard a player's coming games look as a whole: above 1.00 is an easier run than average.
strength_of_schedule.formula: the mean matchup rating of a player's opponents in weeks 15-17 (byes left out)

surface_grass.title: Grass field
surface_grass.explanation: Kicking footing differs a little between grass and turf.
surface_grass.formula: 1 for grass or dessograss, 0 for artificial turf; unknown -> NULL, filled with the training median

tag_threshold_x.title: Tag threshold X
tag_threshold_x.explanation: How far the projection must sit from his current PPG before we tag him.
tag_threshold_x.formula: per season, the X in 0, 0.5 .. 6 with the best Sell-high (Buy-low) precision on the earlier seasons among those tagging at least 3 players per week; never chosen on the season it is used in

target_share.title: Target share
target_share.explanation: The share of his team's passes thrown to a player. Targets are the raw material of receiving points.
target_share.formula: player targets / team targets in that game (nflverse player_stats)

target_share_avg3.title: Target share, last 3 games
target_share_avg3.explanation: How much of the passing game goes to him lately.
target_share_avg3.formula: mean nflverse target_share over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

target_share_last.title: Target share, last game
target_share_last.explanation: The share of his team's passes thrown his way last game.
target_share_last.formula: nflverse target_share in the team's last game, 0 without a stat line (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

target_share_rookie.title: Rookie target share
target_share_rookie.explanation: An early role is the strongest sign of a coming breakout.
target_share_rookie.formula: target share in his rookie season (entry year; S itself for a first-year player)

target_share_s.title: Target share
target_share_s.explanation: His share of the passing game.
target_share_s.formula: his targets / his team's targets in his games of S

targets.title: Targets
targets.explanation: The actual number in the game, counted by ffopportunity over the same plays as its expected value.
targets.formula: fact_opportunity_week.rec_attempt: passes thrown to him (two-point tries excluded), from the same ffopportunity row (fact_opportunity_week), i.e. over the same plays

td_rate_over_expected.title: TD rate over expected
td_rate_over_expected.explanation: Touchdowns beyond what his chances were worth, per pass, carry or target.
td_rate_over_expected.formula: (passing_tds + rushing_tds + receiving_tds - the same three _exp) / (pass_attempts + carries + targets), over the games of one half of a player-season (summed, then divided)

team.title: Team code
team.explanation: An identifier: used to join tables, never as a model feature (a model would memorize who, not learn why).

team_any_a.title: Team ANY/A (QB quality)
team_any_a.explanation: How good his team's passing game was.
team_any_a.formula: his S team's (passing yards + 20 x TD - 45 x INT - sack yards) / (attempts + sacks) in the regular season of S (Pro Football Reference's ANY/A; no model column)

team_change_s1.title: New team
team_change_s1.formula: his week-1 chart team (the team where he has his best offense rank) differs from his S team (his last regular-season game's)

team_epa_per_play.title: Team EPA per play
team_epa_per_play.explanation: How efficient his offense is: good offenses create more points to go around.
team_epa_per_play.formula: mean epa over his team's run and pass plays (no two-point tries) in the season's visible games

team_epa_per_play_neutral.title: Team EPA per play (neutral)
team_epa_per_play_neutral.explanation: Offensive efficiency when the game is close, the fairest view of a team.

team_games_remaining.title: Games remaining
team_games_remaining.explanation: How much season is left to use him.
team_games_remaining.formula: his team's regular-season fixtures after week N (fact_schedule, plus listed cancelled games)

team_games_to_date.title: Team games so far
team_games_to_date.explanation: How many games the team numbers are based on.
team_games_to_date.formula: the as-of team's regular-season games of the season with a final score visible at the as-of

team_pass_rate_neutral.title: Team neutral pass rate
team_pass_rate_neutral.explanation: How pass-heavy his team is when the score does not force it.
team_pass_rate_neutral.formula: share of his team's neutral-situation run and pass plays with pass = 1 (passes, sacks, scrambles)

team_plays_per_game.title: Team plays per game
team_plays_per_game.explanation: Pace: more plays mean more chances for everybody.
team_plays_per_game.formula: his team's run and pass plays (no two-point tries) / its visible games

team_points_per_game.title: Team points per game
team_points_per_game.explanation: How much the team's offense scores: more scoring drives mean more kicks.
team_points_per_game.formula: mean of the entity's as-of team's final scores, per game = mean over the team's regular-season games of the season visible at the as-of (NULL before its first game)

team_rz_stall_rate.title: Red-zone stall rate
team_rz_stall_rate.explanation: The share of red-zone trips that end without a touchdown.
team_rz_stall_rate.formula: stalls / trips of the as-of team this season (red-zone trip = a drive (fact_play.fixed_drive) with a snap at the opponent's 20 or closer (pass, run, field goal, kneel, spike or a penalty snap; two-point tries excluded); stall = a trip whose drive result is not 'Touchdown'); NULL without a trip

team_rz_stalls_per_game.title: Red-zone stalls per game
team_rz_stalls_per_game.explanation: Drives that reach the red zone but stall usually end in a short field goal: kicker points.
team_rz_stalls_per_game.formula: the as-of team's red-zone trips that did not end in a touchdown / its games with play-by-play (red-zone trip = a drive (fact_play.fixed_drive) with a snap at the opponent's 20 or closer (pass, run, field goal, kneel, spike or a penalty snap; two-point tries excluded); stall = a trip whose drive result is not 'Touchdown')

team_rz_trips_per_game.title: Red-zone trips per game
team_rz_trips_per_game.explanation: How often the offense gets inside the opponent's 20-yard line.
team_rz_trips_per_game.formula: the as-of team's red-zone trips / its games with play-by-play (red-zone trip = a drive (fact_play.fixed_drive) with a snap at the opponent's 20 or closer (pass, run, field goal, kneel, spike or a penalty snap; two-point tries excluded); stall = a trip whose drive result is not 'Touchdown')

teammate_role.title: Teammate role
teammate_role.explanation: Where the teammate stands in line: with the WR1 out, the next receiver is 'WR2'.
teammate_role.formula: position + usage rank (baseline carry share + target share, then snap share) among the teammates who play; the absent starters of his position count first; deeper than RB3 / WR4 / TE2 is '<pos>+'

teammate_same_pos_unavailable.title: Teammates out at his position
teammate_same_pos_unavailable.explanation: How many players at his position are out.
teammate_same_pos_unavailable.formula: number of unavailable teammates of his position group

teammate_unavailable.title: Unavailable teammate
teammate_unavailable.explanation: A teammate who is out now: his targets and carries are up for grabs. Each rule is recorded so the app can say why.
teammate_unavailable.formula: a teammate (same as-of team, QB/RB/WR/TE, who played for the team this season) is unavailable at the as-of if ANY of: roster_status = his row on the team's latest visible weekly roster has a status other than ACT, INA, DEV (RES, PUP, SUS, CUT ...), used only in seasons whose roster statuses change from week to week (2016 on: the 2002-2015 rosters repeat one, season-final status on every week); left_team = he was on the team's roster earlier this season but not on its latest visible roster (released or traded); injury_report = the team's latest visible injury report of the season lists him Out or Doubtful; missed_last_game = no offensive snap or stat line in the team's last game after averaging at least 50% snap share in the up to 3 team games before it

temp_f.title: Temperature
temp_f.explanation: Cold air and a hard ball make long kicks shorter.
temp_f.formula: fact_game.temp, else the 'Temp: N' in fact_play.weather; indoors = 70; still unknown outdoors -> NULL, filled with the median of the training rows' outdoor games

tendency_fantasy_link.title: Coach tendency and fantasy targets
tendency_fantasy_link.explanation: Whether an offense's style shows up in fantasy numbers: a team that passes more than expected throws more targets to its receivers the same season, and a little of that carries into the next. Measured, not assumed.
tendency_fantasy_link.formula: Pearson r over completed team-seasons (both sides relative to their season) of a tendency with the team's pass-catchers' targets per game (or full-PPR receiving points per game) the same season and the next season; y_per_x_sd = r x the target's SD: the change per standard deviation of the tendency; 95% season-block bootstrap interval

tendency_percentile.title: Tendency percentile
tendency_percentile.explanation: Where the offense ranks that season: 80 means it passes (or goes for it, or runs no-huddle) more than 80% of the offenses. Early in a season, and for a coach with few games, there is no rank: the sample is too small.
tendency_percentile.formula: 100 x (average rank - 0.5) / rows ranked, among the season's coach-team rows with at least 150 offensive snaps (fourth-down rates: at least 10 choices / 5 short choices); a higher value ranks higher, so for pace a high percentile is a slow offense and the site shows 100 - percentile as 'faster than'

tendency_persistence.title: Does a coach's style carry over?
tendency_persistence.explanation: How well this year's style predicts next year's: 1 = exactly, 0 = not at all. Comparing the coach who moves with the team he left shows whether a tendency belongs to the coach or to the team around him.
tendency_persistence.formula: Pearson r of a team-season's main-coach value (most snaps, at least 400; minus the league that season) with the next one, for three kinds of pairs: same coach and team, same coach at a new team, new coach at the same team; 95% interval from a season-block bootstrap (2,000 draws, fixed seed); completed seasons only

tenure_censored.title: Tenure starts before the data
tenure_censored.explanation: The coach was already in charge when our data begins; his tenure is a minimum.
tenure_censored.formula: the current stint reaches the warehouse's first season (1999), so the true tenure may be longer than tenure_seasons

tenure_seasons.title: Coach tenure
tenure_seasons.explanation: How long the coach has been in charge of this team.
tenure_seasons.formula: seasons of the coach's current stint with the team, this one included: consecutive seasons back from this one in which he coached it a game (coach_game, kickoff <= as-of)

third_season.title: Entering his third season
third_season.explanation: Second-year (rookie season just ended) vs third-year player.

timeout_seconds_wasted.title: Seconds wasted with timeouts in hand
timeout_seconds_wasted.explanation: Clock the team let run when a timeout would have kept its last possession alive, while it kept timeouts it never used.
timeout_seconds_wasted.formula: while down 1-8 in the final 2:00, after an opponent play that leaves K(d', t - 1) < clock <= K(d', -1) (decisive), no team timeout and a runoff (next snap's gap minus the play's measured seconds) >= 10 s; per opponent drive the first k such runoffs, k = the timeouts the team still held at the drive's end

timeouts_unused.title: Timeouts unused in a lost one-score game
timeouts_unused.explanation: The team lost a close game while the opponent ran out the clock, with timeouts still in its pocket. A fact, not always a mistake: see timeout_seconds_wasted.
timeouts_unused.formula: regulation loss by 1-8; the opponent's drive held the game's last snap and had a 4th-quarter snap with <= 120 s where K(d, t) < clock <= K(d, 0) (t >= 1 the team's timeouts); the team's timeouts at that drive's last snap; a case when >= 1

took_over_mid_season.title: Took over mid-season
took_over_mid_season.explanation: The coach replaced someone during this season (usually an interim coach).
took_over_mid_season.formula: the team's first played regular-season game this season had another coach

top_teammate_out.title: A player ahead of him is out
top_teammate_out.explanation: Someone who played ahead of him is out: the classic waiver opportunity.
top_teammate_out.formula: an unavailable same-position teammate averaged a higher snap share than he did over the same games (the teammate's last 3 team games up to his last appearance)

toss_up.title: Toss-up
toss_up.explanation: A decision whose best two options were within the toss-up margin of each other: the model cannot tell them apart with confidence, so it is counted but never graded, whatever the coach chose.
toss_up.formula: WP(best option) - WP(second best) <= decisions.toss_up_margin: counted, never graded

touches_s.title: Touches
touches_s.explanation: Workload; very heavy loads (350+ for a running back) often precede a decline.

train_eligible.title: Usable for training
train_eligible.explanation: Whether a model may learn from this row. A label detail: never a model feature.
train_eligible.formula: window_games >= 2 (PROJECT_SPEC 8.1: weeks with fewer remaining games are left out of training)

two_point_rate.title: Two-point rate
two_point_rate.explanation: How often a two-point try succeeds.
two_point_rate.formula: successful two-point tries / tries in the last 5 seasons before S

vacated_carries_share_s1.title: Vacated carries
vacated_carries_share_s1.explanation: Carries left behind by departed teammates.

vacated_carry_share.title: Vacated carry share
vacated_carry_share.explanation: Carries freed up by teammates who are out.

vacated_share.title: Vacated share
vacated_share.explanation: The part of his team's running plays (passes) the missing starter usually gets: the work that is up for grabs.
vacated_share.formula: the absent starter's mean carry (target) share in the team's games this season in which he played (summed when several starters are out)

vacated_target_share.title: Vacated target share
vacated_target_share.explanation: Targets that teammates who are now out used to get: somebody has to catch them.
vacated_target_share.formula: sum over his unavailable teammates (see teammate_unavailable) of their target_share averaged over the team's last 3 games up to their last appearance (before they became unavailable; games they missed count as 0)

vacated_targets_share_s1.title: Vacated targets
vacated_targets_share_s1.explanation: Targets left behind by departed teammates.
vacated_targets_share_s1.formula: the team's S regular-season targets by players absent from its week-1 chart / the team's S targets

walk_forward.title: Walk-forward backtest
walk_forward.explanation: Grading a model the honest way: every season is predicted by a model trained only on the seasons before it, using only data that was public at each Tuesday's as-of time.
walk_forward.formula: for each test season S: fit only on seasons before S (settings chosen on the last season before S), score every as-of of S from the data public then, no refit during S; the harness refuses any training row of S or later

weather_missing.title: Weather unknown
weather_missing.explanation: Flags the games whose weather was filled in, so the model can treat them apart.
weather_missing.formula: 1 for an outdoor game whose temperature or wind is unknown even after the weather text (then imputed)

weekly_ecr_listed.title: On the weekly expert list
weekly_ecr_listed.explanation: Experts list only the kickers and defenses worth starting.
weekly_ecr_listed.formula: a weekly K or DST page of the season is visible and lists the entity; NULL when no page is visible (before late 2020)

weekly_ecr_rank.title: Weekly expert rank
weekly_ecr_rank.explanation: Where experts ranked it last week.
weekly_ecr_rank.formula: the entity's pos_rank on FantasyPros' latest weekly K or DST ranking of the season visible at the as-of (the Friday before week N's games; late 2020 on); K by gsis_id, DST by team; NULL when not listed or no page

weekly_pos_rank.title: Weekly position rank
weekly_pos_rank.explanation: Where a player's score ranked at his position that week: rank 5 at WR means four receivers scored more. Built from the finished week, so it is outcome data for labels; a feature must rank only the games public at its as-of.
weekly_pos_rank.formula: 1 + the number of players of the same position with more fantasy points that regular-season week, among every player with a stat line (rank 'min': ties share the better rank); position = his point-in-time roster position that week (fact_roster_week.position; without a row that week his latest earlier roster week of the season, else that game's fact_snaps.position); QB/RB/WR/TE only (fullbacks and others are not ranked). Column pos_rank of weekly_finishes

wind_mph.title: Wind
wind_mph.explanation: Wind pushes long kicks off line.
wind_mph.formula: fact_game.wind, else the 'Wind: ... N mph' in fact_play.weather ('calm' = 0); indoors = 0; still unknown outdoors -> NULL, filled with the training median

window_games.title: Games in the label window
window_games.explanation: How many games the player's team has in the window. A label detail: never a model feature.
window_games.formula: len(window_weeks): 3, fewer in the last weeks of a season

window_points.title: Weekly points in the window
window_points.explanation: Week-by-week scores, for reports and eyeballing. A label detail: never a model feature.
window_points.formula: fantasy points of each window week (0 for a week he played without a stat line, NULL for a week he did not play)

window_ranks.title: Weekly ranks in the window
window_ranks.explanation: Week-by-week ranks, for reports and eyeballing. A label detail: never a model feature.
window_ranks.formula: weekly_pos_rank of each window week (NULL where he had no stat line)

window_weeks.title: Label window weeks
window_weeks.explanation: The weeks whose results decide the label. A label detail: never a model feature.
window_weeks.formula: the first 3 regular-season weeks after the as-of week N in which the player's as-of team has a game (its bye weeks skipped), up to the last regular-season week (dim_week.is_last_reg_week)

wins_vs_expected.title: Wins vs market expectation
wins_vs_expected.explanation: Positive: the team has won more than the market expected; negative: fewer.

wopr.title: WOPR (weighted opportunity rating)
wopr.explanation: One number that blends how often a player is targeted with how deep those targets are; a good summary of a receiver's opportunity.

wopr_avg3.title: WOPR, last 3 games
wopr_avg3.explanation: One number for a receiver's recent opportunity.
wopr_avg3.formula: mean nflverse wopr (1.5 x target share + 0.7 x air-yards share) over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

wp.title: Win probability
wp.explanation: The chance the offense wins from this moment, given score, time, field position and more. Garbage time and neutral situations are defined from it.
wp.formula: nflfastR's estimated probability that the team with the ball wins, before the snap

wp_fg.title: WP if kicking a field goal
wp_fg.explanation: The offense's chance to win if it kicks.
wp_fg.formula: P(make) x WP(3 points up, opponent receives the kickoff) + (1 - P(make)) x WP(the opponent's ball at the spot of the kick or its 20); only within the longest field goal made before S

wp_go.title: WP if going for it
wp_go.explanation: The offense's chance to win if it goes for it here.
wp_go.formula: P(convert) x expected WP after a conversion + (1 - P(convert)) x expected WP after a failure (G2 ball-spot tables, G1 WP; fold models of seasons < S)

wp_kick.title: WP if kicking the extra point
wp_kick.explanation: The scoring team's chance to win if it kicks after a touchdown.
wp_kick.formula: PAT rate x WP(+1) + (1 - PAT rate) x WP(+0), the opponent then receiving the kickoff

wp_lost.title: WP lost
wp_lost.explanation: How much win probability a decision gave away by the model's numbers.
wp_lost.formula: WP of the best option - WP of the chosen option (0 when the best was chosen); summed over clear decisions only

wp_lost_per_game.title: WP lost per game
wp_lost_per_game.explanation: A coach's decision cost per game, for the leaderboard.
wp_lost_per_game.formula: (fourth-down + two-point WP lost on clear decisions) / games coached

wp_points.title: WP points
wp_points.explanation: Win probability in percentage points: one WP point is one percentage point of the team's chance to win, by our win-probability model.
wp_points.formula: 100 x a win probability (or a difference of two) on the 0-1 scale

wp_punt.title: WP if punting
wp_punt.explanation: The offense's chance to win if it punts.
wp_punt.formula: G2's punt_expected_wp with the measured kickoff spot after a return touchdown; only from yardlines punts come from

wp_two_point.title: WP if going for two
wp_two_point.explanation: The scoring team's chance to win if it goes for two.
wp_two_point.formula: two-point rate x WP(+2) + (1 - rate) x WP(+0), the opponent then receiving

wpa.title: WPA (win probability added)
wpa.explanation: How much one play or decision changed a team's chance of winning.
wpa.formula: win probability after the play minus before it, for the offense

wrong_call.title: Wrong call
wrong_call.explanation: A clear call where the coach did not choose the option with the highest win probability.
wrong_call.formula: a clear call whose chosen option is not the recommended one (the highest WP); it costs WP lost = WP(best) - WP(chosen)

xfp.title: xFP (expected fantasy points)
xfp.explanation: What an average player would have scored from the same chances (where he was targeted, where he carried the ball). Opportunity is sticky week to week.
xfp.formula: sum over stats of (expected stat x points per unit in config/scoring.yaml): the ffopportunity model's expected passing, rushing and receiving yards, touchdowns, two-point conversions, interceptions and receptions of a player-game (fact_opportunity_week *_exp columns); fumbles and return or fumble-recovery touchdowns have no expected value and add 0. Regression Watch's lists, stability study and backtest (since 2026-10-01, step H6-b2) and the player pages' weekly xFP (since 2026-10-02, step PXFP) score the same per-play expectations from the own walk-forward models instead (own_xfp); the Waiver Radar's features keep ffopportunity's

xfp_avg3.title: xFP, last 3 games
xfp_avg3.explanation: What his recent chances were worth per game, whatever he did with them.
xfp_avg3.formula: mean xfp over the team's last 3 games (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

xfp_garbage.title: xFP in garbage time
xfp_garbage.explanation: What his chances after the game was decided were worth.
xfp_garbage.formula: the expected points of his garbage-time plays (fact_play.is_garbage_time), counted play by play as in play_xfp (NULL without an ffopportunity row)

xfp_last.title: xFP, last game
xfp_last.explanation: Expected fantasy points from his chances last game.
xfp_last.formula: xfp in the team's last game, 0 without a row (team games = regular-season games of the player's as-of team visible at the as-of; last = the most recent, avg3 = mean over the last 3 (fewer early in the season), season = mean over all; a game he missed counts as 0; NULL only when the team has no visible game)

xfp_ng.title: xFP without garbage time
xfp_ng.explanation: What his chances were worth while the game was still in doubt.
xfp_ng.formula: xfp - xfp_garbage: the weekly xFP minus the expected points of his garbage-time targets, carries and passes (the own walk-forward xFP's in Regression Watch and on the player pages)

xfp_per_game_s.title: Expected points per game (own xFP)
xfp_per_game_s.explanation: The points his opportunities were worth to an average player.
xfp_per_game_s.formula: sum of his own walk-forward xFP (Regression Watch, each season from models trained on earlier seasons) over the regular season of S / games_s; NULL before 2009

y_breakout.title: Breakout
y_breakout.explanation: A young player who becomes a fantasy starter.
y_breakout.formula: top-24 WR / top-12 TE / top-24 RB in PPG with 8+ games in S+1 (Breakout population: WR/TE/RB with S - entry year 0 or 1, a game in S, not top-36 WR / top-12 TE / top-24 RB in S)

y_cliff.title: Cliff
y_cliff.explanation: A veteran whose scoring falls by 30% or more.
y_cliff.formula: PPG in S+1 <= 70% of PPG in S with 6+ games in S+1 (Cliff population: 3+ prior seasons, top-36 PPG at his position with 8+ games in S); NULL when y_missed

y_cliff_or_missed.title: Cliff or missed
y_cliff_or_missed.explanation: The sensitivity run: missing most of the next season counts as a cliff.

y_hit.title: Waiver hit
y_hit.explanation: What the Waiver Radar predicts: will this player be startable soon?
y_hit.formula: n_starter_finishes >= 1: at least one starter finish in the label window (the next 3 regular-season weeks after the as-of week N in which his as-of team plays; a bye is skipped and extends the window, the season's last regular-season week ends it), counting only stat lines public strictly after the as-of

y_missed.title: Missed next season
y_missed.explanation: Injury, benching, release or retirement: kept apart from the Cliff (owner, 2026-10-02).
y_missed.formula: fewer than 6 games in S+1 (Cliff population)

y_start.title: Streamer label: a starter next week
y_start.explanation: Would the kicker or defense you pick up on Tuesday have been worth starting in the very next game? Streaming is a one-week decision.
y_start.formula: the entity's week N+1 fantasy points (config/scoring.yaml kicking: / defense:) rank in the top (teams x lineup slots) at its position among everyone who played that week: top 12 K and top 12 DST in this league (ties at the cutoff all count); NULL on a bye, after the last regular-season week, or while week N+1 is not final; a kicker without a kick in week N+1 is False

y_sustained.title: Sustained hit
y_sustained.explanation: A stricter target: a player who stays startable, not a one-week spike.
y_sustained.formula: n_starter_finishes >= 2: as y_hit, but in at least two window weeks

yac.title: Yards after the catch
yac.explanation: Yards he gained with the ball after catching it.
yac.formula: receiving_yards - air_yards over his caught targets (two-point tries excluded), from fact_opportunity_pass

yac_exp.title: Expected yards after the catch
yac_exp.explanation: Yards after the catch an average receiver would have gained on the same catches; yac - yac_exp is 'YAC over expected'.
yac_exp.formula: yards_after_catch_exp over his caught targets (two-point tries excluded)

yac_over_expected.title: YAC over expected
yac_over_expected.explanation: Yards after the catch beyond what an average receiver gains on the same catches.
yac_over_expected.formula: (yac - yac_exp) / receptions, over the games of one half of a player-season (summed, then divided)

yardline_100.title: Yards to the end zone
yardline_100.explanation: Field position: 1 = at the opponent's goal line, 99 = backed up at your own 1.
yardline_100.formula: yards between the line of scrimmage and the opponent's goal line

yards_per_team_pass_att_s.title: Yards per team pass attempt
yards_per_team_pass_att_s.explanation: Production per team dropback: rewards both role and efficiency.
yards_per_team_pass_att_s.formula: his receiving yards / his team's pass attempts in his games of S

yards_per_touch_s.title: Yards per touch
yards_per_touch_s.formula: (rushing + receiving yards) / touches in S; NULL under 20 touches

yards_per_touch_trend.title: Yards-per-touch trend
yards_per_touch_trend.explanation: Negative: he is getting less out of each touch than before.
yards_per_touch_trend.formula: yards_per_touch_s - the mean of the S-1 and S-2 values that exist

ydstogo.title: Yards to go
ydstogo.explanation: The distance the offense still needs; 3rd and 1 is far better than 3rd and 12.
ydstogo.formula: yards needed for a first down (or a touchdown)

years_exp.title: Years of experience
years_exp.explanation: Seasons in the league before this one.
years_exp.formula: his latest visible roster row's years_exp

z_margin.title: Lead in standard deviations of what is left
z_margin.explanation: A random-walk view of the game: how many 'typical swings of the remaining time' the offense is ahead by, counting the ball and the spread.
z_margin.formula: (score_differential + drive_value + posteam_spread x t) / (13.5 x sqrt(t) + 1), t = share of regulation left
